originalText:
Broodling
For as long as humans have existed, there have been
broodlings. A self-interested, secretive people, they adopt
human forms to influence events in their favor. A few use
their shapeshifting abilities to hunt humans in towns and
cities, while others orchestrate vast conspiracies to keep
themselves well fed and protected from discovery. They
enjoy manipulating mortals and construct elaborate ruses
to trick them, often with fatal consequences.
A broodling can pass for human, though close inspection
reveals the flaws in its disguise. Hairless and corpulent, with
waxy flesh, broodlings don’t quite fit into their clothes, and
they continually shed tiny worms and beetles. Many don dark
glasses to conceal their strange eyes, which never point in the
same direction. Should a broodling become injured, it sheds
its fleshy exterior and reveals its horrid true nature: a seething
cloud of gray flies rushes out from the deflating flesh.
Broodlings speak High Archaic and the Common Tongue.

---

Bestiary
BROODLING DIFFICULTY 100
Size 1 monster
Perception 15 (+5); darksight
Defense 15; Health 80; Insanity —; Corruption 4
Strength 10 (+0), Agility 15 (+5), Intellect 12 (+2), Will 13 (+3)
Speed 8
Immune damage from cold, disease, and poison; asleep,
diseased, fatigued, poisoned
Shed Skin When the broodling becomes injured, it
immediately sheds its human form and assumes its
swarm form. It can return to its human form, using a
triggered action on its turn, if its damage total is less
than its Health.
Swarm Form In this form, the broodling is a Size 2 cloud
of stinging and biting insects. It moves only by flying
and can move freely through openings large enough
to permit a Size 1/8 or larger creature and can move
through other creatures’ spaces. Other creatures can
move into its space, which is difficult terrain.
		 While in swarm form, the broodling takes half damage
from effects that use an attack roll and takes double
damage from effects that require it to make a challenge
roll. It is immune to being grabbed and being knocked
prone.
Stinging Cloud While the broodling is in its swarm form, all
creatures, other than broodlings or swarms, are impaired
while in the broodling’s space or within 1 yard of it.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Touch (melee) +5 with 1 boon (4d6)
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Sudden Dissolution When the broodling takes damage

originalText:
Burrowing Centipede
Burrowing centipedes are horrific parasites that chew their
way into other creatures and nest inside their bodies for
protection. A burrowing centipede might remain inside its
host for weeks or even months, emerging only to feed.
BURROWING CENTIPEDE DIFFICULTY 5
Size 1/4 animal
Perception 15 (+5); darksight
Defense 15; Health 15; Insanity 0; Corruption 0
Strength 8 (–2), Agility 15 (+5), Intellect 5 (–5), Will 6 (–4)
Speed 14
ATTACK OPTIONS
Mandibles (melee) +5 (2d6 plus Burrow on attack roll 20+
against a living target)
Burrow The centipede burrows inside the target, which
becomes its host. It remains inside until the host becomes
incapacitated or the centipede makes an attack.
		 While the centipede is inside it, the host is impaired.
The centipede moves with it and cannot perceive
anything outside the host’s body. The centipede can
attack only that host, and its attack roll results in an
automatic success. Doing so causes the centipede to exit
from the host’s body into an open space of its choice
within 1 yard of the host.
		 A creature with the academic (medicine) profession
and a healer’s kit can attempt to remove the centipede
from its host by spending 1 hour and making an Intellect
challenge roll with 3 banes. On a success, it extracts the
centipede, which dies. On a failure, the host takes 1d6
damage.

originalText:
Catoblepas
A catoblepas resembles a bison with thick armored plates
covering its back and a shaggy head equipped with two
small, curling horns. Despite their appearance, herds of
catoblepases are uncommon; most roam the Desolation
singly, scouring the landscape for the rare green growth
clumped around the few oases in the blasted lands.
Though normally docile, if threatened or surprised, a
catoblepas reacts with a blast of poisonous green vapor
from its nostrils that petrifies anything it kills.

---

Bestiary
CATOBLEPAS DIFFICULTY 100
Size 2 monster
Perception 11 (+1)
Defense 18; Health 100; Insanity 0; Corruption 0
Strength 15 (+5), Agility 10 (+0), Intellect 6 (–4), Will 9 (–1)
Speed 8
ATTACK OPTIONS
Horns (melee) +5 with 1 boon (2d6)
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Poisonous Cloud The catoblepas exhales a toxic cloud in a
6-yard-long cone that spreads from a point it can reach.
The cloud partially obscures the area and remains for 1
round or until dispersed by wind.
Each living creature in the area that is not a catoblepas
must make a Strength challenge roll with 1 bane, taking
6d6 damage on a failure or half the damage on a
success. A creature incapacitated by this damage dies
instantly and turns into a stone statue.
		 After the catoblepas uses Poisonous Cloud, it cannot
do so again for 1 round.

originalText:
Changeling
Called impostors, spies, and worse, changelings live in
fear of being discovered for what they truly are. They were
created by mischievous faerie to take the place of stolen
humans, and they live as those people until the magic that
made them begins to fail. In their true form, changelings
are often hideous, since their bodies are fashioned from
plants, dirt, bits of wood, and rock. For this reason, as well
as human distrust, changelings constantly wear disguises.
A changeling can become anyone it sees: a member of the
watch, a local priest, a bartender who knows the names
of all her patrons, a wizened elder, or a young child.
Changelings have trouble making meaningful connections
with others or developing interests independent of the
individuals whose forms they borrow. As a result, they
drift from one goal to the next, caring little whether they
accomplish it or not.
Humans know about changelings and ascribe all manner
of sinister qualities to them. In some lands, especially those
near the realms of faerie, people must submit to the test
of iron to prove they are what they appear to be. The test
is simple: merely take and hold a piece of iron. Faerie and
their kin cannot abide its touch and are impaired while
they remain in contact with it.
Most changelings speak the Common Tongue.

---

Bestiary
CHANGELING DIFFICULTY 10
Size 1 faerie
Perception 12 (+2); shadowsight
Defense 13 (soft leather); Health 17; Insanity 0; Corruption 0
Strength 9 (–1), Agility 12 (+2), Intellect 11 (+1), Will 9 (–1)
Speed 10
Immune damage from disease; charmed, diseased
Iron Vulnerability A changeling is impaired while it is in
contact with iron.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Bronze Scimitar (melee) +2 with 1 boon (2d6 + 1)
Bow (long range) +2 with 1 boon (2d6)
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Steal Identity The changeling uses an action, or a triggered
action, on its turn to alter its appearance to match
that of a target living creature it can see within short
range. The target must be Size 1 or 1/2 and have a
humanoid shape of flesh and blood. The changeling’s
body changes so it looks like the target, though its
clothing and possessions remain unchanged. The effect
lasts until the changeling uses this talent again. If it
becomes incapacitated or comes into contact with
iron, the changeling immediately reverts to its normal
appearance. When the changeling steals a creature’s
identity, its attack rolls against that creature are made
with 1 boon while it has that creature’s appearance.

originalText:
Clockwork
Clockworks are machines imbued with mortal souls stolen
from the Underworld. All clockworks, regardless of form,
feature keys in places they can’t reach. When the key stops
turning, they become insensate objects until someone else
cranks them up again.
Clockworks typically speak the Common tongue. The
clockwork presented here has a human form and functions
as a soldier.
CLOCKWORK DIFFICULTY 10
Size 1 clockwork
Perception 10 (+0)
Defense 14 (small shield); Health 32; Insanity 0; Corruption 0
Strength 12 (+2), Agility 8 (–2), Intellect 10 (+0), Will 10 (+0)
Speed 8
Immune damage from disease or poison; asleep, diseased,
fatigued, poisoned
Key A clockwork has a key somewhere on its body that
it cannot reach. When the key is cranked and turning,
the clockwork counts as a creature, becoming an object
when the key stops. Its key stops turning when the
clockwork becomes incapacitated. It also stops turning
at the end of any round in which the clockwork got a
total of 0 or lower on an attack roll or challenge roll.
		 While it is an object, the clockwork cannot use actions,
move, talk, or perceive its surroundings. Any creature
that can reach the clockwork can use an action to wind
up the key; if not incapacitated, the clockwork becomes
a creature once more.
Grind the Gears A clockwork can increase the number of
actions it can use on its turn by one. When it finishes
its turn, roll a d6. On an odd number, the clockwork
becomes an object at the end of the round.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Sword (melee) +2 with 1 boon (2d6 + 2)

originalText:
Cockatrice
A cockatrice looks like a miniature two-legged dragon with
the head of a rooster. It is ill-tempered and dangerous: a
single peck from its beak can harden flesh into stone. The
frozen forms of creatures that ran afoul of a cockatrice
decorate the landscape around its lair.
COCKATRICE DIFFICULTY 25
Size 1 monster
Perception 11 (+1)
Defense 14; Health 40; Insanity 0; Corruption 0
Strength 12 (+2), Agility 12 (+2), Intellect 6 (–4), Will 10 (+0)
Speed 6; flier
ATTACK OPTIONS
Beak (melee) +2 with 1 boon (4d6 plus Petrify on attack
roll 20+ against a living creature)
Petrify The target becomes slowed for 1 minute as its body
grows heavy. If the target is already slowed in this way, it
instead takes 4d6 extra damage. A target that becomes
incapacitated by the cockatrice’s attack turns into a
statue, dying instantly.
Construct
Constructs include a variety of creatures fashioned
from nonliving materials. A construct can have whatever
appearance its maker desires: it might be an ordinary
object animated by magic, a simulacrum of another
creature woven from threads of magic, or a machine
built in an engineer’s workshop to fulfill a specific
purpose.
Appendage
A construct attacks with any part of its body that can
function as a weapon, or simply slams its body into
enemies. Those constructed to look like creatures might
use fists, horns, or feet. A wardrobe rams opponents or
batters them with its doors. An animated rug moves like
a serpent, rearing back and darting forward to pummel
enemies.

Appendage (melee) +3 (2d6)
Demon
The Void belongs to the demons. These malevolent
shadows flit through the endless darkness and infest the
wreckage of the untold worlds destroyed by the Demon
Lord. As slaves to the Ender of All Things, evil and madness
consume these entities. Demons’ obsession with killing
and destroying makes them utterly unreasonable and
unpredictable.
Demons lack physical forms. Only when they enter
the universe do they gain bodies, almost always of a
horrid and monstrous aspect, as if assembled from
discarded parts by an idiotic and insane god.
Under their own power, demons cannot pierce the
boundary that separates the Eternal Darkness from the
universe beyond. They scour the edges for the rare gaps
where their master’s influence bleeds through or rely on
foolish mortals to summon them and let them loose to
visit ruin on the world. Once they have escaped the
Void, demons do not willingly return. Only the utter
annihilation of their physical forms or powerful
magic can cast them back whence they came.
Demons’ malevolent essence interacts with
the magic pervading the universe to create their
physical forms, so they are naturally resistant
to magical effects. They bring some of the Void’s
darkness with them when they materialize, plunging
their environs into shadow. Even so, their forms are
eerily visible; even creatures that cannot clearly see
them are subject to the demons’ horrifying trait.
Demonic Talent
Every demon takes on a unique appearance when
it materializes. The more powerful demons gain
unique abilities, represented by random rolls on
the Demonic Talents table. Instead of a demonic
talent, you can instead increase the demon’s
Health as directed in its statistics box.

Spell Defense A demon takes half damage from spells and
makes any challenge roll to resist a spell with 1 boon.
A creature attacking the demon with a spell makes its
attack roll with 1 bane.
Demonic Shadows Lit areas out to 2 yards around the
demon become shadows.
Demonic Talent Roll once on the Demonic Talents table or
increase the demon’s Health by 20.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Natural Weapon (melee) +7 with 2 boons (3d6)
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Frenzied Attack The demon attacks two different targets
with its natural weapon, making each attack roll with
1 bane.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Void Step The demon uses an action or a triggered action
on its turn to teleport to a space it can see within
medium range. Roll a d6. On a roll of 1, the demon cannot
use Void Step again for 1 minute.
Demonic Possession
If a creature goes mad as a result of gaining Insanity from
a demon’s horrifying trait, the demon can use a triggered
action to possess that creature. The demon makes a Will
attack roll against the triggering creature’s Will. On a success,
it disappears and enters the creature’s body, replacing the
creature’s Intellect and Will with its own and supplanting the
creature’s personality. The demon makes a prisoner of the
possessed creature’s soul and learns everything the creature
knows and remembers.
The demon can choose to hide within the possessed
creature, allowing the creature’s soul to take charge of the
body once again. The possessed creature has no recollection
of what happened while the demon was in control and does
not know of the possession. The demon can reassert control
at any time it chooses.
A creature possessed by a demon typically displays some
physical manifestation of the evil presence. It might reek
of rotting meat, expel foul substances, become sexually
aggressive, display weird markings on its flesh or assume an
unusual color, become afflicted with boils, sores, and bruises,
or have some other disturbing characteristic.
A possessing demon can be forced out of the creature’s
body, usually by magic. Once forced out, the demon must
make a Will challenge roll. On a success, it appears in an
open space of its choice within 10 yards of that creature. On a
failure, the demon disappears into the Void.

Bestiary
Demonic Talents
d20 Talent

Incarnation of Death The radius of the demon’s Demonic Shadows increases by 1 yard. At the end of each round, each
living creature in the area that is not a demon must make a Strength challenge roll. On a failure, the creature takes 2d6
damage.

Foment Discord Once per round, the demon can use a triggered action on its turn to make a Will attack roll against the
Will of one target creature within medium range of it. On a success, the target becomes consumed by hate for 1 round.
While consumed by hate, it must take the first turn it can and use an action to charge or make an attack with a weapon
against a target chosen by the demon.

Demon Seed When the demon gets an attack roll total of 20 or higher with its natural weapon and exceeds the target’s
Defense by 5 or more, it attempts to implant its seed in the target’s body. The target must make an Agility challenge roll
with 1 bane. On a failure, the target becomes implanted with a demon seed. The seed takes 1d6 rounds to mature. At the
end of each round until then, the target takes 1d6 damage and must make a Will challenge roll. On a failure, the target is
dazed from pain for 1 round. At the end of the round in which the seed matures, the target takes 3d6 damage and a tiny
demon tears free from its body, entering an open space within 1 yard of it.

Poisonous The demon’s claws, fangs, or other natural weapons drip with venom. It gains the poisonous trait (see
Customizing Creatures).

Dread The demon uses an action or a triggered action on its turn to send a wave of terror into an 8-yard-long cone
originating from a point it can reach. Each creature in the area must make a Will challenge roll. On a failure, the creature
gains 1 Insanity. If the creature is already frightened, it also becomes stunned for 1 minute. Once the demon uses Dread, it
cannot do so again for 1 hour.

Weapon of Chaos The demon wields a weapon of chaos, a manifestation of its dark will, in place of its natural weapon.
Attack rolls with this weapon are made with 1 boon, dealing 1d6 + its natural weapon damage. In addition, a creature
that takes damage from the weapon of chaos gains 1 Corruption.

Erratic At the end of each round, roll a d6. On an odd number, the demon is dazed for 1 round. On an even number, the
demon can take both a fast turn and a slow turn during the next round, making attack rolls and challenge rolls with 1 boon.

Legion The demon’s form is a fusion of several smaller demons. The first time it takes any damage, it collapses into a pile
of small demons. Divide the original demon’s Difficulty by 50 to determine how many appear; each enters an open space
within 1 yard of the original demon’s space and can take the next available turn. The new demons do not have this talent.

Stench At the end of each round, each living creature within short range of the demon must make a Strength challenge
roll. On a failure, the creature becomes impaired for 1 round.
10 Plague-Bearer The demon carries a loathsome disease. It gains the infectious trait (see Customizing Creatures).

Barbed Tendrils The demon uses an action to launch 1d6 barbed tendrils from its body, dividing them as it chooses
between any number of target creatures within short range of it. For each tendril, the demon makes a Strength attack
against the target’s Agility. On a success, the tendril punches into the target’s body, dealing 1d6 damage. Until it frees
itself, the target cannot move away from the demon and is pulled along (remaining at the same distance) if the demon
moves away from it. The target can free itself by destroying all the tendrils attached to it. Each tendril has Defense 5
and Health 5. Once the demon uses Barbed Tendrils, it cannot do so again for 1 hour.

Pincers When the demon gets a success on an attack roll using its natural weapon, it can use a triggered action to grab
the target.

Infested Tiny animals, such as rats or frogs, infest the demon’s body. When the demon takes damage from a weapon, 1d6
tiny animals spill out of it and attack the creature that damaged their host. Each enters an open space within 1 yard of the
demon’s space and can take the next available turn. Once the demon uses Infested, it cannot do so again for 1d6 rounds.

Spiked Tail The demon uses an action or a triggered action on its turn to make a Strength attack roll with 1 boon against
the Defense of one target creature within the demon’s reach + 1. On a success, the target takes 2d6 damage.

Flatulence The demon uses an action or a triggered action on its turn to expel a foul cloud of gas from its orifices.
The cloud spreads out in an 8-yard-long cone from a point the demon can reach. Each creature in the area must make
a Strength challenge roll. On a failure, the creature becomes poisoned while it remains in the cloud and for 1 round
after it leaves. While poisoned in this way, the creature is also dazed. Once the demon uses Flatulence, it cannot do
so again for 1 hour.
16 Wings The demon can fly at its listed speed.

Spellcaster (Minor) The demon has Power 1. Choose one tradition. The demon knows one rank 0 spell and two rank 1
spells from that tradition. If the demon already has a Spellcaster talent, instead increase the demon’s Health by 20.

Spellcaster (Major) The demon has Power 2. Choose one tradition. The demon knows one rank 0 spell, two rank 1 spells,
and one rank 2 spell from that tradition. If the demon already has this talent or a Spellcaster talent from a higher roll,
instead increase the demon’s Health by 20.

Spellcaster (Superior) The demon has Power 3. Choose one tradition. The demon knows one rank 0 spell, two rank 1
spells, two rank 2 spells, and one rank 3 spell from that tradition. If the demon already has this talent or a Spellcaster
talent from a higher roll, instead increase the demon’s Health by 20.

Spellcaster (Diverse) The demon has Power 3. Choose two traditions. The demon knows one rank 0 spell, one rank 1
spell, one rank 2 spell, and one rank 3 spell from each tradition. If the demon already has this talent, instead increase its
Health by 20.

against the target’s Agility. On a success, the tendril punches into the target’s body, dealing 1d6 damage. Until it frees
itself, the target cannot move away from the demon and is pulled along (remaining at the same distance) if the demon
moves away from it. The target can free itself by destroying all the tendrils attached to it. Each tendril has Defense 5
and Health 5. Once the demon uses Barbed Tendrils, it cannot do so again for 1 hour.

Pincers When the demon gets a success on an attack roll using its natural weapon, it can use a triggered action to grab
the target.

Infested Tiny animals, such as rats or frogs, infest the demon’s body. When the demon takes damage from a weapon, 1d6
tiny animals spill out of it and attack the creature that damaged their host. Each enters an open space within 1 yard of the
demon’s space and can take the next available turn. Once the demon uses Infested, it cannot do so again for 1d6 rounds.

Spiked Tail The demon uses an action or a triggered action on its turn to make a Strength attack roll with 1 boon against
the Defense of one target creature within the demon’s reach + 1. On a success, the target takes 2d6 damage.

Flatulence The demon uses an action or a triggered action on its turn to expel a foul cloud of gas from its orifices.
The cloud spreads out in an 8-yard-long cone from a point the demon can reach. Each creature in the area must make
a Strength challenge roll. On a failure, the creature becomes poisoned while it remains in the cloud and for 1 round
after it leaves. While poisoned in this way, the creature is also dazed. Once the demon uses Flatulence, it cannot do
so again for 1 hour.
16 Wings The demon can fly at its listed speed.

Spellcaster (Minor) The demon has Power 1. Choose one tradition. The demon knows one rank 0 spell and two rank 1
spells from that tradition. If the demon already has a Spellcaster talent, instead increase the demon’s Health by 20.

Spellcaster (Major) The demon has Power 2. Choose one tradition. The demon knows one rank 0 spell, two rank 1 spells,
and one rank 2 spell from that tradition. If the demon already has this talent or a Spellcaster talent from a higher roll,
instead increase the demon’s Health by 20.

Spellcaster (Superior) The demon has Power 3. Choose one tradition. The demon knows one rank 0 spell, two rank 1
spells, two rank 2 spells, and one rank 3 spell from that tradition. If the demon already has this talent or a Spellcaster
talent from a higher roll, instead increase the demon’s Health by 20.

Spellcaster (Diverse) The demon has Power 3. Choose two traditions. The demon knows one rank 0 spell, one rank 1
spell, one rank 2 spell, and one rank 3 spell from each tradition. If the demon already has this talent, instead increase its

originalText:
Dragon
Dragons come in many different shapes and sizes. Some
have colorful or drab scales, while others feature hair,
spines, and other characteristics. All dragons have the same
general shape: a sinuous body with a long tail that extends
to about twice the body’s length. Two leathery wings extend
out from the shoulder blades, large enough to carry the
heavy creature into the air. A dragon’s large head tips a long,
flexible neck and boasts a crown of horns and an enormous
maw filled with sharp teeth. All dragons can belch up a
noxious fluid similar to naphtha that ignites when ejected
from their mouths.
Dragons can be found in all climates and terrains, from
coastal caves to the depths of forests to caverns deep under
the mountains. They are solitary creatures and emerge
from their lairs only to feed; they eat anything they catch.
Dragons prize shiny, glittering things, and many decorate
their lairs with fantastical treasures.
DRAGON DIFFICULTY 500
Size 2 or 3 frightening monster
Perception 19 (+9); truesight
Defense 23; Health 160; Insanity 2; Corruption 3
Strength 17 (+7), Agility 13 (+3), Intellect 14 (+4), Will 16 (+6)
Speed 16; flier (swoop)
Immune damage from fire; charmed, dazed, frightened,
sleep, stunned
Spell Defense A dragon takes half damage from spells and
makes any challenge roll to resist a spell with 1 boon. A
creature attacking the dragon with a spell makes the
attack roll with 1 bane.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Claws (melee) +7 with 3 boons (2d6)
Teeth (melee) +7 with 3 boons (3d6 plus 1d6 from fire)

---

Bestiary
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Flurry of Attacks The dragon attacks twice with its claws
and once with its teeth.
Spew Fire The dragon sprays flames in a 10-yard-long cone
from a point it can reach. Everything in the area takes
4d6 + 5 damage. Each creature in the area must make
an Agility challenge roll with 2 banes. On a failure, the
creature takes 4d6 + 5 extra damage and catches fire.
Once the dragon uses Spew Fire, it cannot do so again
for 1 round.

originalText:
Dread Mother
Dread mothers inhabit the most far-flung hinterlands
of the civilized world. They inspire terror as they wing
through the night skies, descending to feed and to deposit
their young in the living flesh of their victims. A dread
mother has a human-shaped form with great feathery
wings, similar to those of moths, spreading from its back.
It has shriveled arms and legs and a heavy abdomen
distended by the eggs it carries.
When a dread mother attacks, it flies toward a living
creature and unhinges its jaw to let loose a long, prehensile
tongue that ends in a sharp spike. The tongue injects a
toxin that renders its victim defenseless. The dread mother
squats over the fallen creature and uses a special organ to
implant the eggs inside the wound. Its belly now empty, the
monster flutters off to feed elsewhere, leaving its young to
eat their way free from the host.
DREAD MOTHER DIFFICULTY 25
Size 1 frightening monster
Perception 12 (+2)
Defense 14; Health 30; Insanity 3; Corruption 2
Strength 12 (+2), Agility 14 (+4), Intellect 7 (–3), Will 10 (+0)
Speed 10; flier (Flutter)
ATTACK OPTIONS
Tongue (melee) +4 (2d6 plus Poison)
Poison The target must make a Strength challenge roll with 2
banes. On a failure, it becomes poisoned for 1 minute. While
poisoned in this way, the target is defenseless. If it is already
poisoned in this way, it instead takes 4d6 extra damage.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Implant Eggs The dread mother implants 1d6 eggs in
one target defenseless creature within its reach that
is not already so implanted. The eggs remain inside
that creature until they hatch or are removed. While a
creature is host to the eggs, it is impaired.
		 After 2d6 hours, the implanted eggs hatch and tiny
larvae eat their way out of the host’s body, appearing
in open spaces within 1 yard of it. The host takes 2d6
damage and gains 1 Insanity per egg; if it becomes
incapacitated by this damage, it dies instantly. Each larva
is size 1/8 and has Health 1.

---

Bestiary
		 Removing an egg requires 1 hour of work by a
character with the academic (medicine) profession using
a healer’s kit. At the end of this time, the attempting
character makes an Intellect challenge roll. On a success,
the egg is safely removed. On a failure, the egg breaks,
killing the larva but dealing 1d6 damage to the host.
END OF THE ROUND
Flutter Roll a d6. The dread mother flies a number of
yards equal to the number rolled, but not farther than its
Speed. This movement does not trigger free attacks.

originalText:
DrYad
Dryads live in the depths of untamed woods. These willful,
capricious sprites dance through the trees, silvery laughter
echoing weirdly as they pass. They lure humans who catch
their fancy into their homes, imprisoning them for months
or years before releasing the captives from their charms.
Dryads hide within their chosen trees unless they choose
to reveal themselves; finding one that doesn’t want to be
discovered is almost impossible. When a dryad steps forth,
it resembles a young and beautiful woman, with pointed
ears, glittering eyes, and hair that matches the colors of the
leaves on its tree.
Dryads speak Elvish.
DRYAD DIFFICULTY 50
Size 1 faerie
Perception 15 (+5); shadowsight
Defense 18; Health 20; Insanity 2; Corruption 1
Strength 10 (+0), Agility 14 (+4), Intellect 12 (+2), Will 16 (+6)
Speed 10; Tree to Tree
Immune damage from disease; charmed, diseased
Spell Defense A dryad takes half damage from spells and
makes any challenge roll to resist a spell with 1 boon.
A creature attacking the dryad with a spell makes the
attack roll with 1 bane.
Treebound A dryad is bound to a particular tree. It is impaired
while it is more than long range away from that tree.
Charming Beauty On first seeing a dryad, a living creature
must make a Will challenge roll with 1 bane. On a failure,
the creature becomes charmed until the dryad that
charmed it becomes incapacitated or uses a triggered
action on its turn to remove the affliction. On a success,
it becomes immune to that dryad’s Charming Beauty
until after that creature completes a rest.
Lure When the dryad ends its move on its turn, each
creature charmed by it and within medium range of it
moves up to half its Speed toward the dryad.
Tree to Tree While moving, a dryad can enter one tree’s
space and instantly exit from that tree or from a different
tree within medium range of the tree it entered.
Iron Vulnerability A dryad is impaired while it is in contact
with iron.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Rooting Touch (melee) +4 with 1 boon (2d6 + 1 and the
target becomes immobilized for 1 round)
MAGIC
Power 5
Enchantment presence (6), charm (3), mind bondage (2)
Nature magic acorns (6), overgrowth (3), ensnaring vines
(2), brambles (2), form of the oak guardian (1)

originalText:
Dwarf
Dwarfs delve deep into the earth, digging for gold, silver,
gemstones, and other treasures from the unyielding stone.
A people of short stature and broad build, they are strong
and hardy, able to withstand the hardships of their work
and the depths into which they descend. Most dwarfs,
both male and female, have extensive facial hair, which
they wear in beards and mustaches braided or greased into
fanciful shapes. Dwarfs have long memories and never
forget a slight. They despise goblins and trolls, and their
grudges sometimes impel them to attack on sight.
Legend holds the dwarfs were not always as they are
today. Grimnir, their maker, fashioned them to be tall,
beautiful, and powerful. But their vanity was the dwarfs’
undoing. They saw the gods not as their masters, but as
their rivals. They built a great tower to climb through
the skies so they could lay siege to heaven and take the
gods’ thrones for themselves. For their hubris, Grimnir
cursed them. He stripped from them their beauty and
stature, leaving them and all their descendants a stunted,
embittered people. The god doomed them to grub for the
treasures of earth instead of seeking the glories of heaven,
and so all dwarfs are born with a lust for gold and gems.
Dwarfs speak Dwarfish and the Common Tongue.
DWARF DIFFICULTY 10
Size 1/2 dwarf
Perception 11 (+1); darksight
Defense 16 (mail, small shield); Health 16; Insanity 0;
Corruption 0
Strength 12 (+2), Agility 9 (–1), Intellect 10 (+0), Will 10 (+0)
Speed 8
Robust Constitution A dwarf takes half damage from
poison and makes challenge rolls with 1 boon to avoid or
remove the poisoned affliction.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Pick (melee) +2 with 1 boon (1d6 + 2)
Crossbow (long range) –1 with 1 boon (2d6)
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Shake It Off The dwarf heals 4 damage and removes
one of the following afflictions: fatigued, impaired, or
poisoned. Once it uses Shake It Off, the dwarf can’t do so
again until it completes a rest.

originalText:
Elf
The lords and ladies of the hidden kingdoms, elves
abandoned the mortal world long ago for the wondrous
realms spun into being with their great magical power, such as
Alfheim or the Lands of the Ever Young. A few retreated into
the deep wilderness, unwilling to surrender their homelands
to the talking beasts that stink of iron. Most elves prefer their
isolation, but some leave the bright lands to walk in the world
and gaze with wonder or horror on mortal works.
Elves are slender and comely people, with heart-shaped
faces, canted eyes, pointed ears, and androgynous features.
They dress in clothing made from strange and impossible
materials such as shadows, moonbeams, or a lover’s breath.

---

Bestiary
All elves appreciate beautiful things. They have no
sense of ownership; an elf sees nothing wrong with taking
something that catches his or her fancy, whether an object
such as a painting or the eyes of a young child.
Elves speak Elvish. Most also know the Common Tongue
or High Archaic.
ELF DIFFICULTY 10
Size 1 faerie
Perception 14 (+4); shadowsight
Defense 15 (soft leather); Health 40; Insanity 1; Corruption 0
Strength 9 (–1), Agility 14 (+4), Intellect 13 (+3), Will 11 (+1)
Speed 12
Immune damage from disease; charmed, diseased
Spell Defense An elf takes half damage from spells and
makes any challenge roll to resist a spell with 1 boon. A
creature attacking the elf with a spell makes the attack
roll with 1 bane.
Iron Vulnerability An elf is impaired while in contact with iron.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Bone Scimitar (melee) +4 with 1 boon (1d6 + 1)
Bone Long Knife (melee) +4 with 1 boon (1d6)
Bow (long range) +4 with 1 boon (1d6)
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Swift Shot When the elf makes an attack with its bow, it
can use a triggered action to repeat the attack against
the same or a different target.
Twin Strike The elf attacks once with its bone scimitar and once
with its bone long knife. It makes each attack roll with 1 bane.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Countless Doors The elf can use a triggered action at
any time to teleport to an open space it can see within
medium range. Once it uses Countless Doors, the elf
cannot do so again for 1 minute.

originalText:
Fungal Hulk
Fungal hulks and their mite offspring are mobile colonies
that prowl the deep caverns in search of living hosts in
which they can implant their spores. A fungal hulk looks
like an enormous mushroom with a drooping, perforated
cap, a thick trunk with two armlike appendages ending in
heavy knobs, and two rubbery legs.
When a fungal hulk kills a creature, it injects the corpse
with spores. After 1d6 hours, 1d6 fungal mites emerge. A
fungal mite matures into a fungal hulk in 1d6 days.
FUNGAL HULK DIFFICULTY 50
Size 2 fungus
Perception 11 (+1); sightless
Defense 9; Health 50; Insanity —; Corruption —
Strength 15 (+5), Agility 9 (–1), Intellect 5 (–5), Will 15 (+5)
Speed 12
Immune asleep, blinded, dazed, deafened, fatigued,
frightened, stunned
Corrosive Spores When the fungal hulk takes damage from
a weapon, it releases a cloud of spores that spread into a
3-yard-radius sphere centered on a point within its space. The
cloud partially obscures its area and remains until the end of
the round or until dispersed by wind. Any living non-fungus
creature that is in the cloud when it appears or that enters it
takes 2d6 damage, or half the damage with a success on a
Strength challenge roll. Once the fungal hulk uses Corrosive
Spores, it cannot do so again until after the end of the round.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Appendage (melee) +5 with 2 boons (2d6 + 3)
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Double Attack The fungal hulk attacks twice with its appendage.

originalText:
Fury
Furies fly out from the depths of Hell to visit doom on
oathbreakers and traitors, on their own or at the behest
of their infernal masters. Once a fury sets its sights on a
victim, it pursues the offending mortal to the ends of the
earth, determined to drag the soul to Hell.
Furies appear as winged women dressed in diaphanous
gowns spotted with blood, their long hair held back in
braids. They would be beautiful were it not for the hatred
contorting their features. All furies wield fiery swords.
Furies speak High Archaic.

---

Bestiary
FURY DIFFICULTY 250
Size 1 frightening faerie (devil)
Perception 13 (+3); truesight
Defense 18; Health 75; Insanity —; Corruption 4
Strength 16 (+6), Agility 14 (+4), Intellect 10 (+0), Will 15 (+5)
Speed 12; flier (swoop)
Immune damage from disease and poison; asleep,
diseased, frightened, poisoned
Spell Defense A fury takes half damage from spells and
makes any challenge roll to resist a spell with 1 boon. A
creature attacking the fury with a spell makes the attack
roll with 1 bane.
Iron Vulnerability A fury is impaired while it is in contact
with iron.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Blazing Blade (melee) +6 with 2 boons (2d6 + 2 plus 2d6
from fire)
Burning Bow (long range) +4 with 2 boons (2d6 + 1 plus
2d6 from fire)
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Twin Strike The fury attacks twice with its blazing blade or
its burning bow. It makes each attack roll with 1 bane.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Oath of Ruin The fury can use an action or a triggered
action when it takes damage to swear to destroy one
target creature it can see. Until it or the target becomes
incapacitated, the fury makes attack rolls with 1 boon
against the target. Once the fury uses Oath of Ruin, it
cannot do so again until the target is dead.
END OF THE ROUND
Dread Each creature that is not a faerie within 1 yard of
the fury must make a Will challenge roll. On a failure, the
creature becomes frightened for 1 round. If it is already
frightened, it instead becomes dazed for 1 round.
Genie
When the universe sprang into
existence eons ago, it brought with it
bodiless entities, awakened
by creation’s magic. Such
spirits usually drift through
the worlds, unseen, unfelt,
unnoticed but for a tingling of
the skin, a sensation of someone
or something nearby, or a faint
noise that has no obvious source.
Genies live in dancing flames,
stirring breezes, hulking mountains,
and crashing waves, heedless of the
oblivious mortals.
Rarely do genies trouble other
creatures, unless compelled by magic.
Practitioners of elemental magic summon
them to learn the spells that manipulate these primal
forces. When summoned, a genie assumes a physical
form infused with elemental power to become a wild,
dangerous entity.

Earth Stride An earth genie ignores the effects of moving

Empowered by Earth When an earth genie would take

as a bonus to its Health. The bonus lasts for 1 minute.

3. While its Health is 120 or higher, its Size becomes 4.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Fist (melee) +10 (6d6, or 36 to an object); the genie makes
the attack roll with 1 boon if the target is in contact with
earth, sand, or stone.
END OF THE ROUND
Unruly Earth Each creature that is not a genie on the ground
within short range of the earth genie must make an Agility
challenge roll with 1 bane, falling prone on a failure. A creature
that is already prone instead takes 2d6 damage. Objects on
the ground in the area automatically take 2d6 damage.
What at first looks like a stack of rocks and dirt reveals its
true nature when it moves. The rocks making up the genie’s
body behave like limbs, streams of dust and small stones
spilling from its earthen form. Black chips of glittering
obsidian serve as its eyes.

originalText:
Ghastly Chorus
A ghastly chorus is made from stripping the faces of a dozen
or more victims from their skulls and fusing them into a
sheet of stretched skin. It moves by fluttering and lurching
over the ground, eyes flicking back and forth, its many
mouths yawning wide as they whisper dire secrets of the
afterlife.
Ghastly choruses lurk in old ruins and cemeteries,
where dabblers in the dark arts ruminate over the
forbidden knowledge they have accumulated.
The chorus serves its maker as a herald,
announcing the sovereignty of its master to
any who stumble into the lair.
The deboned heads used to create a ghastly
chorus retain scraps of memory from their lives.
Their mouths whisper or shriek in the Common
Tongue or, rarely, High Archaic. The abomination
craves conversation and gibbers madly at anyone who
will listen, lashing out violently at those who won’t. Its mad
pronouncements and horrific appearance assault mortal
minds, leaving their owners gasping in terror.
GHASTLY CHORUS DIFFICULTY 50
Size 2 horrifying undead
Perception 15 (+5); darksight
Defense 12; Health 50; Insanity —; Corruption —
Strength 10 (+0), Agility 12 (+2), Intellect 11 (+1), Will 13 (+3)
Speed 8; Creep
Immune damage from cold, disease, and poison; asleep,
diseased, fatigued, immobilized, poisoned, prone
Amorphous A ghastly chorus can move freely through
openings wide enough to permit the passage of water, and
it can move through spaces occupied by other creatures.
Dazing Horror Creatures that gain Insanity from the
ghastly chorus’s Mournful Song are also dazed while
they are frightened in this way. A creature that is already
dazed is instead stunned for the duration.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Mouths (melee) +0 with 4 boons (6d6 + 6 plus Crushing
Grab on attack roll 20+)
Crushing Grab The target is grabbed. If it was already
grabbed, the target instead takes 3d6 extra damage.
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Mournful Song Each creature within medium range of the
ghastly chorus that can hear it must make a Will challenge
roll with 1 bane. On a failure, the creature gains 1 Insanity.
END OF THE ROUND
Creep The ghastly chorus moves up to half its Speed.

originalText:
Ghoul
Most societies forbid humans to knowingly feed on other
humans. To do so invites a horrid curse: transformation
into a ghoul.
Ghouls are corpse-eaters, shunned for their unspeakable
appetites. They prowl graveyards, breaking into tombs
and digging up coffins to get at the choice morsels within.
Eternally hungry, ghouls eat any flesh, no matter how
rancid or putrid. However, when given the choice, they
favor fresh meat pulled from the bones of children.
A ghoul adopts the likeness of the last creature it ate. As
its unholy appetite grows, it reverts to its usual gaunt and
sickly form, its crusted maw filled with pointed black teeth
and a forked, sore-ridden tongue.
Ghouls speak the Common Tongue.
GHOUL DIFFICULTY 25
Size 1 frightening monster
Perception 12 (+2); shadowsight
Defense 15; Health 40; Insanity 5; Corruption 4
Strength 11 (+1), Agility 13 (+3), Intellect 8 (–2), Will 11 (+1)
Speed 8
Immune damage from disease or poison; diseased, poisoned
Fear of the Gods A ghoul makes attack rolls with 1 bane
against a creature wearing or wielding a holy symbol.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Claws and Teeth (melee) +3 with 1 boon (2d6 + 3 plus
Drink Blood on attack roll 20+)
Drink Blood If the target is a living creature of flesh and
blood, it takes 1d6 extra damage and becomes fatigued
for 1 minute. While fatigued in this way, the target is
also slowed. If it was already fatigued, it instead takes
another 1d6 extra damage.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Unholy Feast The ghoul eats one dead creature it can
reach, which requires concentrating for 1 minute. At
the end of this time, the ghoul utterly consumes the
corpse and assumes the creature’s appearance for 24
hours. While wearing this new form, the ghoul loses its
frightening trait.

originalText:
Giant
Giants are primitive, backward, and incredibly stupid.
They pay little attention to where they go and leave a trail
of smashed houses, flattened wagons, and partly eaten
livestock when wandering through settled lands.
A typical giant stands about 15 feet tall and weighs about
2,000 pounds. It looks like an enormous human with a
slouched posture and exaggerated features: a broad nose,
drooping eyebrows, and a slack mouth filled with stained
teeth the size of shields. Most giants eschew clothing,
though the more modest might strap livestock, living or
dead, over their nether regions, or don carnival tents.
Giants speak the Trollish language. More intelligent
giants might also know the Common Tongue.
GIANT DIFFICULTY 100
Size 3 or larger giant
Perception 10 (+0)
Defense 15; Health 100; Insanity 1; Corruption 2
Strength 17 (+7), Agility 11 (+1), Intellect 8 (–2), Will 13 (+3)
Speed 12
Stupidity A giant makes Intellect attack rolls and challenge
rolls with 1 bane. Creatures make attack rolls against the
giant’s Intellect with 1 boon.
Crushing Footfalls When a giant moves into a space
occupied by a creature on the ground, the creature must
make an Agility challenge roll. On a failure, it takes 3d6
damage and falls prone. If it’s already prone, it takes 1d6
extra damage. A creature makes this roll once per round
per giant regardless of how many times the giant moves
through its space.
Giantfall The giant deals damage equal to 2d6 × its Size to
everything in the area where it falls. A creature can make
an Agility challenge roll with a number of banes equal
to the giant’s Size (minimum 1 bane). On a success, the
creature takes half the damage and moves to the nearest
open space outside the area. On a failure, the creature
becomes trapped under the giant’s body.
		 A trapped creature is prone, blinded, immobilized, and
totally covered. It can use an action to make an Agility
challenge roll with a number of banes equal to the giant’s
Size + 1. On a success, the creature moves to the nearest
open space and removes all afflictions imposed by Giantfall.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Fist (melee) +7 with 3 boons (5d6)
Boulder (long range) +7 with 1 boon (3d6)

slouched posture and exaggerated features: a broad nose,
drooping eyebrows, and a slack mouth filled with stained
teeth the size of shields. Most giants eschew clothing,
though the more modest might strap livestock, living or
dead, over their nether regions, or don carnival tents.
Giants speak the Trollish language. More intelligent
giants might also know the Common Tongue.
GIANT DIFFICULTY 100
Size 3 or larger giant
Perception 10 (+0)
Defense 15; Health 100; Insanity 1; Corruption 2
Strength 17 (+7), Agility 11 (+1), Intellect 8 (–2), Will 13 (+3)
Speed 12
Stupidity A giant makes Intellect attack rolls and challenge
rolls with 1 bane. Creatures make attack rolls against the
giant’s Intellect with 1 boon.
Crushing Footfalls When a giant moves into a space
occupied by a creature on the ground, the creature must
make an Agility challenge roll. On a failure, it takes 3d6
damage and falls prone. If it’s already prone, it takes 1d6
extra damage. A creature makes this roll once per round
per giant regardless of how many times the giant moves
through its space.
Giantfall The giant deals damage equal to 2d6 × its Size to
everything in the area where it falls. A creature can make
an Agility challenge roll with a number of banes equal
to the giant’s Size (minimum 1 bane). On a success, the
creature takes half the damage and moves to the nearest
open space outside the area. On a failure, the creature
becomes trapped under the giant’s body.
		 A trapped creature is prone, blinded, immobilized, and
totally covered. It can use an action to make an Agility
challenge roll with a number of banes equal to the giant’s
Size + 1. On a success, the creature moves to the nearest
open space and removes all afflictions imposed by Giantfall.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Fist (melee) +7 with 3 boons (5d6)
Boulder (long range) +7 with 1 boon (3d6)

Goblin
Cast out from the realms of faerie long ago, goblins now
make their way in the mortal world. They occupy the
bottom rung of the social ladder, performing the work no
one else is willing to do. Many goblins delight in making
mischief, and the worst of their kind live as thieves,
scoundrels, and troublemakers.
Goblins reproduce like rats. They live in crowded
conditions in underground warrens, often in human cities,
using scraps and stolen materials. No two goblins are exactly
alike. Most stand around 3 feet tall and weigh about 40 or 50
pounds, but all have a unique characteristic that sets them
apart. Horns, fangs, snouts, tails, blotchy skin, extra digits or
eyes, and worse mar their forms.
Goblins speak the Common Tongue and Elvish.

Size 1/2 faerie
Perception 12 (+2); shadowsight
Defense 14 (soft leather); Health 8; Insanity 1; Corruption 1
Strength 8 (–2), Agility 13 (+3), Intellect 11 (+1), Will 9 (–1)
Speed 10
Immune damage from disease; charmed, diseased
Iron Vulnerability A goblin is impaired while it is in contact
with iron.
Sneaky A goblin attempting to hide or move silently makes
the Agility challenge roll with 1 boon.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Spear (melee) +3 (1d6)
Bow (long range) +3 (1d6)
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Spring Away When a creature the goblin can see gets a
failure on an attack roll against the goblin’s Defense or
Agility, the goblin can use its triggered action to retreat.

originalText:
Gorgon
The Witch-King created the gorgons from his brides, whose
beauty was unmatched by any in the world. He gifted
them with eternal life, but to keep their vanity in check, he
also cursed them, transforming them into monstrosities
whose gaze turned the living to stone statues. Somehow,
the gorgons survived the Witch-King’s defeat and scattered
across the Empire’s lands.
An echo of the beauty that earned their place as the
Witch-King’s brides still lingers in gorgons’ shapely upper
bodies and striking features. But the rest of their forms are
monstrous: crowns of eyeless serpents emerge from their
heads and long serpent tails replace their legs.
Gorgons dwell in old ruins, under cities, or in remote
wilderness areas where they pass the endless years in
isolation. Some offer guidance to mortals who dare
approach, conferring on them the wisdom accumulated
over their long lives.
A gorgon’s gaze retains power for 1d6 days after the
gorgon dies, provided its eyes remain intact. A creature
wielding the gorgon’s head can subject others to the
gorgon’s Petrifying Appearance and Petrifying Gaze.
Gorgons communicate in High Archaic.
GORGON DIFFICULTY 500
Size 1 monster
Perception 17 (+7); darksight
Defense 18; Health 120; Insanity —; Corruption 5
Strength 12 (+2), Agility 16 (+6), Intellect 12 (+2), Will 17 (+7)
Speed 8
Immune charmed, compelled, dazed, frightened, stunned
Petrifying Appearance On first seeing a gorgon, a creature
must make a Will challenge roll with 2 banes. On a failure,
the creature gains 1 Insanity, cannot avert its eyes from the
gorgon, and becomes slowed for a number of rounds equal
to the creature’s Insanity total. Whether it gets a success or a
failure, it cannot again be affected by that gorgon’s Petrifying
Appearance until after that creature completes a rest.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Scimitar (melee) +6 with 3 boons (2d6 + 1)
Longbow (long range) +6 with 3 boons (2d6 + 1)
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Twin Strike The gorgon attacks twice with its scimitar
or longbow. It makes each attack roll with 1 bane.
Serpent Hair The gorgon uses an action or a triggered
action on its turn to attack with the serpents crowning
its head. One target creature within the gorgon’s reach
must make an Agility challenge roll with 1 bane, or
with 3 banes if it averted its eyes. On a failure, the
target takes 2d6 damage, becomes poisoned for
1 minute, and cannot avert its eyes for 1 round.
If the target is already poisoned in this way, it
instead takes 2d6 extra damage.
END OF THE ROUND
Epic Recovery The gorgon removes one
affliction from itself.
Petrifying Gaze Each creature within medium range of the
gorgon that can see it must either use a triggered action
to avert its eyes from the gorgon or make a Strength
challenge roll with 1 bane. For 1 round, a creature that
averts its eyes makes attack rolls with 2 banes, and other
creatures make attack rolls against it with 2 boons.
		 A creature that gets a failure on the Strength challenge
roll takes 4d6 + 20 damage and becomes slowed for
1 minute. If the creature is already slowed, it instead
becomes immobilized. A creature that is incapacitated
by this damage dies instantly, transformed into a stone
statue.
Epic Adversary Roll 1d3 + 1 to determine how many actions
the gorgon can use during the next round. The gorgon can
use these actions during any turn and can do so before its
enemies act. Each time the gorgon uses an action, it can
move up to its Speed before or after the action.

originalText:
Gremlin
Cunning mischief-makers, gremlins delight in creating
chaos. Their mere presence causes even the best-laid
plans to go awry. Gremlins followed the goblins out of the
Hidden Kingdoms and now wreak havoc on human cities.
Explosions, misfires, and constructs that behave erratically
are all signs of a gremlin infestation.
Technology attracts gremlins. A gremlin wants nothing
more than to take a device apart to see how it works. When
it puts it back together again, though, the item never seems
to work quite right and has a tendency to break at the most
inopportune times.
Gremlinsaretiny human-shapedcreatureswith grayskin
andspindlybodies,standing8inchestallandweighingnomore
thanapoundortwo.Theyoftenhaveonefeatureof unusual
size,suchasatooth,ear,or nose.Most gremlinsforgoclothing.
Gremlins speak Elvish.
GREMLIN DIFFICULTY 5
Size 1/4 faerie
Perception 13 (+3); shadowsight
Defense 15; Health 5; Insanity 3; Corruption 1
Strength 8 (–2), Agility 15 (+5), Intellect 11 (+1), Will 9 (–1)
Speed 8
Immune damage from disease; charmed, diseased
Spell Defense A gremlin takes half damage from spells and
makes any challenge roll to resist a spell with 1 boon. A
creature attacking the gremlin with a spell makes the
attack roll with 1 bane.
Iron Vulnerability A gremlin is impaired while it is in
contact with iron.
Vexing Presence Each creature that is not a faerie and is
within short range of the gremlin makes attack rolls and
challenge rolls with 1 bane.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Teeth (melee) +5 with 1 boon (1 plus Curse)
Curse If the target is not a faerie, it must make a Will
challenge roll with 3 banes. On a failure, the target
becomes cursed for 1 minute. While cursed, whenever
the target makes an attack roll or a challenge roll, it must
roll twice and use the lower number.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Jinx The gremlin uses an action or a triggered action on its
turn to choose one target object within short range of it that
is neither worn nor carried. The target takes 1d6 damage.
Break When a creature within short range of the gremlin
makes an attack roll using a weapon that is not enchanted,
the gremlin can use a triggered action to make an Intellect
challenge roll. On a success, the triggering weapon takes
damage equal to its Health and breaks.

originalText:
Hag
Nymphs are wilderness faerie of surpassing beauty.
But when a nymph’s joy becomes sorrow and bitterness
replaces happiness, hate causes the nymph’s beauty to
wither and die. What’s left is a horror called a hag. Green-
skinned and warty, it is a monstrous reflection of the
nymph’s former self, intent on making everyone else as
miserable as itself.

---

Bestiary
Hags live in dark, foreboding forests, wastelands, and
other desolate areas. They creep through the night hours,
luring children from their beds and stealing them away.
Their vile magic withers crops, sickens livestock, spoils
milk, and brings bad luck.
Hags speak Elvish.
HAG DIFFICULTY 500
Size 1 horrifying faerie
Perception 16 (+6); shadowsight
Defense 19; Health 80; Insanity —; Corruption 5
Strength 15 (+5), Agility 11 (+1), Intellect 16 (+6), Will 16 (+6)
Speed 8
Immune damage from disease; asleep, charmed, dazed,
diseased, stunned
Spell Defense A hag takes half damage from spells and makes
any challenge roll to resist a spell with 1 boon. A creature
attacking the hag with a spell makes the attack roll with 1 bane.
Iron Vulnerability A hag is impaired when in contact with iron.
Mind-Bending Horror A creature that gains Insanity
from seeing a hag also becomes compelled while it is
frightened in this way.
See Magic A hag sees auras around creatures, objects, and
places affected by magic.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Claws (melee) +5 with 3 boons (4d6)
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Double Attack The hag attacks twice with its claws.
Accursed Eye The hag uses an action or a triggered action
on its turn to make a Will attack roll against the Strength
of one target creature it can see within medium range of
it. On a success, the target becomes impaired for 1 minute.
Accursed Sleep The hag makes a Will attack roll against
the Strength of one target impaired creature it can see
within medium range of it. On success, the target falls
asleep for 1 minute. At the end of this time, the hag can
use a triggered action if it is within medium range of
the target to make a Will attack roll against the target’s
Will. On a success, the target remains asleep for as long
as the hag wishes or until the hag is incapacitated.
Wychfire The hag hurls a ball of green fire at one target
creature within medium range of it, making a Will attack
roll against the target’s Agility. On a success, the target
takes 6d6 damage.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Change Shape The hag uses an action or a triggered
action on its turn to transform into a young human
man or woman of a pleasing appearance. While in
this form, the hag loses its horrifying trait and cannot
use Streaming Smoke; it can use its other attacks and
talents. It remains in this form until it uses a triggered
action at any time to return to its normal form.
Streaming Smoke The hag uses an action or a triggered
action on its turn to transform its body into a roiling
cloud of smoke, fly up to its Speed, and then resume its
normal form. While in this form, the hag is immune to all
damage, can move freely through openings wide enough
to permit the passage of air, and can move through
spaces occupied by other creatures.
MAGIC
Power 4
Curse hex (5), frighten (2), weakness (2), swine (1)
Enchantment presence (5), bewitch (2), charm (2), compel (2)
Forbidden harm (5), hateful defecation (2), tongue rip (2),
desire’s end (1), soul exchange (1)
END OF THE ROUND
Epic Recovery The hag removes one affliction from itself.
Epic Adversary Roll 1d3 + 1 to determine how many actions
the hag can use during the next round. The hag can use
these actions during any turn and can do so before its
enemies act. Each time the hag uses an action, it can
move up to its Speed before or after the action.

originalText:
Halfling
Halflings are diminutive farmers living on the outskirts of
human cities. Their idyllic communities, neat and orderly,
produce much of the foodstuffs on which human nations
depend. Halflings pride themselves in their work, live simply,
and have few ambitions beyond enjoying the time afforded
to them. They are fiercely independent and self-sufficient.
Halflings are cousins to humans, similar in all ways except
height. They stand about 3 feet tall and weigh about 50 pounds.
Halflings have the same range of coloration that humans have.
Halflings speak the Common Tongue.

---

Bestiary
HALFLING DIFFICULTY 1
Size 1/2 halfling
Perception 10 (+0)
Defense 14 (hard leather, small shield); Health 10;
Insanity 0; Corruption 0
Strength 10 (+0), Agility 11 (+1), Intellect 10 (+0), Will 9 (–1)
Speed 10
ATTACK OPTIONS
Spear (melee) +1 (1d6)
Bow (long range) +1 (1d6)
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Good Fortune Whenever a creature within short range of the
halfling rolls a 1 on any die, the halfling can use a triggered
action to let the creature ignore the roll and roll again.
Uncommon Courage When the halfling becomes
frightened, it can use a triggered action to make a Will
challenge roll. On a success, it removes the frightened
affliction.

originalText:
Harpy
Sweet, alluring voices call travelers to their destruction.
They belong to the harpies, a hideous race of accursed
faerie that despise mortals and feed on any they get in
their grasp. Harpies have the wings, tails, and talons of
ravens merged with the torso of nymphs. Beneath the
feces, blood, and hateful behavior, harpies are quite
beautiful.
The harpies were once the loveliest of the nymphs, but
with great beauty came great vanity. They believed they
were greater and more alluring than the Faerie Queen
herself. The Faerie Queen, upon hearing of their boasting,
dismissed them from her court and sent them flying away
as ravens, whose shape still disfigures their forms.
Harpies speak Elvish.
HARPY DIFFICULTY 50
Size 1 faerie
Perception 12 (+2); shadowsight
Defense 15; Health 30; Insanity 3; Corruption 3
Strength 10 (+0), Agility 15 (+5), Intellect 9 (–1), Will 13 (+3)
Speed 10; flier (swoop)
Iron Vulnerability A harpy is impaired while it is in contact
with iron.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Talons and Teeth (melee) +5 with 2 boons (3d6 plus
Painful Compulsion)
Painful Compulsion If living, the target must make a Will
challenge roll. On a failure, it becomes compelled for as
long as the harpy concentrates. On a success, it becomes
immune to that harpy’s Painful Compulsion until that
creature completes a rest.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Seductive Song The harpy uses an action or a triggered
action on its turn to begin singing. It continues to sing
for 1 round and can take only triggered actions during
that time. Each creature that is within or that moves into
long range of a singing harpy must make a Will challenge
roll, with 1 bane for each singing harpy within range
beyond the first.
On a failure, the creature gains 1 Insanity and becomes
charmed for a number of rounds equal to its Insanity
total. While charmed in this way, the creature must take
the first turn it can each round and use an action to
rush toward the nearest singing harpy by the shortest
available route. Once the creature is within short range
of a singing harpy, it stops moving and becomes stunned
until it is no longer charmed.
		 On a success or after removing the charmed affliction,
the creature becomes immune to all harpies’ Seductive
Song until after it completes a rest.
Harvester
Harvesters haunt the Empire’s oldest cities. Direct
descendants of some ancient society, most likely struck
down by offended gods, they perpetuate their existence by
stealing what they need from humans. When something
breaks in a harvester’s body, it replaces the defective
part with whatever it can take until it looks like it has
been cobbled together from a dozen or more creatures.
Harvesters hide their grotesqueness behind heavy clothing
to help them move among their victims without attracting
attention to themselves.

originalText:
ORGAN FILCH DIFFICULTY 10
Size 1 horrifying harvester
Perception 14 (+4); shadowsight
Defense 12; Health 30; Insanity —; Corruption 3
Strength 11 (+1), Agility 12 (+2), Intellect 14 (+4), Will 13 (+3)
Speed 12
ATTACK OPTIONS
Scalpel (melee) +2 with 2 boons (2d6)
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Extract Organ The organ filch steals an organ from a target
incapacitated or defenseless living creature within its
reach, killing the creature instantly. The filch gains a 2d6
bonus to Health until it completes a rest.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Skittering Dance The filch uses an action or a triggered
action on its turn to move up to its Speed. This
movement does not trigger free attacks.
Organ filches scour the shadowed streets of densely
populated cities for vagrants from which they harvest
fresh parts to replace their failing organs. They open up
their victims with long scalpels and carry bottles filled
with preservative fluid to hold their harvests until they
can return to their lairs and install the stolen flesh in their
bodies.
An organ filch goes about covered by a hooded canvas
cloak that is stained with blood from previous hunts.
Beneath is a ghastly figure wrapped in snug linens and
wearing elaborate headgear fitted with lenses to help it
perform surgery.
Organ filches speak High Archaic.

TEAR THIEF DIFFICULTY 50
Size 1 horrifying harvester
Perception 14 (+4); darksight
Defense 17; Health 40; Insanity —; Corruption 4
Strength 12 (+2), Agility 17 (+7), Intellect 10 (+0), Will 12 (+2)
Speed 12
Immune blinded
ATTACK OPTIONS
Long Knife (melee) +7 with 2 boons (3d6 plus Extract Tears)
Extract Tears If living, the target must make a Will
challenge roll with 1 bane. On a failure, it gains 1 Insanity
and the tear thief heals 1d6 damage. If the total of the
challenge roll is 0 or lower, the tear thief also plucks out
one of the target’s eyes.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Hide in Shadows The tear thief can attempt
to hide when it is in an area at least partially
obscured by shadows, even if it is being
observed.
Skittering Dance The tear thief uses an action
or a triggered action on its turn to move
up to its Speed. This movement does not
trigger free attacks.
Harvesters discovered that replacing every part
of their bodies numbed their ability to feel and to
experience emotion. After extensive study, they learned to
concoct an elixir made from human tears that lets them
feel again, if only for a short while. Tear thieves extract
tears by causing their victims to experience horrific pain.
A tear thief wears black leather clothing along with a
heavy coat, white gloves, a top hat, and black lenses over its
eyes. It carries a thin knife with a serrated edge designed to
maximize the victim’s suffering.
Tear thieves speak High Archaic.

originalText:
Hell Swine
Hell swine are a breed of ill-tempered hogs that grow to
obscene size. Vicious and temperamental, they destroy
their habitats and kill just about anything they can catch.
Hell swine have thick, leathery hides, gleaming red eyes,
and tufts of black hair rising from their backs. They gore
their foes with their sharp tusks.
Beastmen have had some success in training hell swine
to serve as steeds, though the beasts are unreliable and can
turn on riders with no warning.

Perception 9 (–1); shadowsight
Defense 16; Health 60; Insanity 2; Corruption 0
Strength 16 (+6), Agility 11 (+1), Intellect 7 (–3), Will 12 (+2)
Speed 12
Ferocious When a hell swine would become incapacitated, roll

ATTACK OPTIONS
Tusks (melee) +6 with 2 boons (3d6)
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Vicious Rebuke When the hell swine takes damage, it can
use a triggered action to attack a randomly determined
creature with its tusks.

hidden kingdoms of the faerie, where they live as slaves to
the elf lords and ladies. They are given to frequent bouts
of madness that manifest as random acts of senseless
violence, and often fight on the front lines in defense of the
faerie realms.
Unlike goblins, who have wildly varied appearances,
hobgoblins are identical, regardless of gender. Each one
stands exactly 5 feet, 4½ inches tall and weighs 166 pounds.
All have thick bellies, spindly limbs, and heavy jowls that
hang to their shoulders.
Hobgoblins speak Elvish.
HOBGOBLIN DIFFICULTY 5
Size 1 faerie
Perception 10 (+0); shadowsight
Defense 15 (brigandine, large shield); Health 23; Insanity 1;
Corruption 0
Strength 13 (+3), Agility 11 (+1), Intellect 9 (–1), Will 11 (+1)
Speed 10
Immune damage from disease; charmed, diseased
Iron Vulnerability A hobgoblin is impaired while it is in
contact with iron.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Cleaver (melee) +3 with 1 boon (1d6 + 2)

---

Bestiary
END OF THE ROUND
Frenzy If the hobgoblin is not in a frenzy, roll a d6. On
a roll of 6, the hobgoblin goes into a frenzy that lasts
for 1 minute. Until the frenzy ends, the hobgoblin deals
1d6 extra damage with its attacks and is immune to the
frightened affliction, and other creatures make attack
rolls against it with 1 boon.

originalText:
Hood
Hoods were created by a secret society known as the Cabal
of the Black Sun, a largely forgotten group of dark wizards
set on finding immortality. They employ hoods as spies,
thieves, and assassins.
Hoods haunt city streets on fell errands for their
inscrutable masters. They don heavy black cloaks that
seem to drink the light and render them nearly invisible
when in shadows or darkness. They say little and seem
skilled in magic.
The few who have managed to see a hood clearly report it
has craggy features covered by a thick mustache and beard,
much like a dwarf. Only removing their cloaks reveals the
awful truth about hoods’ nature. Rather than skulls, they
have great glass orbs filled with murky liquid. Lamprey-
like creatures swim inside the glass vessels, presumably
controlling the hoods’ actions.
Hoods speak High Archaic.
HOOD DIFFICULTY 25
Size 1/2 monster
Perception 15 (+5); darksight
Defense 15 (hard leather); Health 30; Insanity 3; Corruption 1
Strength 11 (+1), Agility 13 (+3), Intellect 11 (+1), Will 12 (+2)
Speed 10
ATTACK OPTIONS
Long Knife (melee) +3 with 2 boons (2d6)
Dagger (melee or short range) +3 with 2 boons (1d6)
Hand Crossbow (medium range) +3 with 2 boons (1d6 plus
Shadow Poison)
Shadow Poison The target must make a Strength
challenge roll. On a failure, it becomes poisoned for 1
minute. While poisoned in this way, the target is also
blinded. If it was already poisoned, it just takes 3d6
extra damage instead.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Hide in Shadows The hood can attempt to hide when it is
in an area at least partially obscured by shadows, even if
it is being observed.
Shadow Step When the hood is in an area obscured
by shadows or darkness, it can use an action or use
a triggered action on its turn to teleport to another
area obscured by shadows or darkness within medium
range.
MAGIC
Power 1
Shadow nightfall blade (2), darkness (1), shadow dart (1)

originalText:
Jack-o'-Lantern
Glowing wisps flicker and dance across the moors. From a
distance, they look like torches or lanterns, but at close range
they are revealed to be nothing of the sort but in fact plumes
of pale fire that bob in the air. When a living creature comes
close, the flame turns bright orange and assumes the form of
a leering face that moves to incinerate anything it can reach.
Jack-o’-lanternsare faerie of malevolentdispositionand
wicked intent. Theylove tolure travelersintodangerandwatch
themburn. Theydonotspeak,thoughtheyunderstandElvish.
JACK-O’-LANTERN DIFFICULTY 250
Size 1/4 horrifying faerie
Perception 15 (+5); truesight
Defense 20; Health 60; Insanity —; Corruption 2
Strength 8 (–2), Agility 20 (+10), Intellect 8 (–2), Will 10 (+0)
Speed 16; flier (swoop; can’t fall)
Immune damage from disease; charmed, diseased, prone
Iron Vulnerability A jack-o’-lantern is impaired while it is in
contact with iron.
Mind-Bending Horror A creature that gains Insanity from
seeing a jack-o’-lantern also becomes compelled while it
is frightened this way.
Burst of Flame Once per round, when a jack-o’-lantern
takes damage, flames burst in a 2-yard-radius sphere
centered on a point within 1 yard of it. Each creature in
the area other than the jack-o’-lantern must make an
Agility challenge roll, taking 3d6 damage on a failure.
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Fey Fire The jack-o’-lantern makes an Agility attack roll
against the Agility of one target creature within 2 yards of
it. On a success, the target takes 3d6 damage. If the total of
the attack roll is 20 or higher, the target also catches fire.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Elude When a creature gets a failure on an attack roll
against the jack-o’-lantern’s Defense or Agility, the jack-
o’-lantern can use a triggered action to retreat. Then roll
1d6. On an even number, the jack-o’-lantern regains the
ability to use a triggered action this round.

originalText:
Killing Mist
Fogplaystricksonthesenses.Sometimestheshadowglimpsed
fromthecorneroftheeyeisnothingmorethana harmless
illusionbroughtonbytheshiftingclouds.Sometimes,though,
there’sreasontoheed thepricklingofthehairsonthebackof
theneck,thecolddreadspreadingthrough theguts,and the
certaintythatthereissomethingelseinthemist—something
utterlymalevolentandnot ofthisworld.
Killing mist appears as a great bank of red-tinged fog that
spills over the ground, plunging the world into pale gloom
as it creeps along. In its depths one can make out weird,
distorted images of impossible shapes accompanied by mad
laughter and strings of words in a deep, muttering voice.
The killing mist never lingers long, dissipating almost as
quickly as it appeared. In the clearing air, one might spot a
few pale, dry bones, all that remains of the unlucky victims
of the entity’s repast.
Killing mist typically conceals itself inside a larger bank
of mundane fog, looking like a particularly dense region of
mist. It haunts shorelines and the surface of waters where
doldrums are common.
KILLING MIST DIFFICULTY 250
Size 10 frightening undead
Perception 20 (+10); sightless
Defense 5; Health 100; Insanity —; Corruption —
Strength —, Agility 5 (–5), Intellect 6 (–4), Will 6 (–4)
Speed 6; flier, Flowing Fog
Immune damage from cold, disease, and poison; asleep,
blinded, charmed, dazed, diseased, fatigued, frightened,
poisoned, prone, stunned, and any effect that would
change the killing mist’s shape
Misty Form A killing mist takes half damage from weapons
and double damage from fire. It makes challenge rolls
to resist Fire spells with 1 bane. Other creatures can
move through and end their movement in its space. The
killing mist totally obscures its area. A killing mist ignores
difficult terrain and can move freely through openings
wide enough to permit the passage of air, but it treats
liquid water as a solid object.
		 Once per round, when exposed to wind created by
magic, the mist takes 4d6 damage and is moved 1d6
yards in the direction the wind is blowing.
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Feed Each creature within the killing mist’s space must
make a Strength challenge roll with 3 banes. On a failure,
the creature takes 6d6 + 5 damage and becomes fatigued
for 1 minute. While fatigued this way, the creature is
slowed. If it is already fatigued from some other source, it
becomes slowed and takes 2d6 extra damage.
END OF THE ROUND
Flowing Fog Roll a d6. On an even number, the mist moves
a number of yards equal to the roll in a direction of its
choice.
Bewildering Mist Each living creature within the mist’s
space must make a Will challenge roll. On a failure,
the creature gains 1 Insanity and becomes dazed for
1 round. A creature driven mad by the mist also becomes
defenseless until the madness ends.

originalText:
Lash Crawler
Clinging to walls and ceilings, lash crawlers might pass
for spiders. Close observation, though, reveals that their
bodies are bloated, pulsing eyeballs, each suspended on
seven long, hair-like legs. Lash crawlers spontaneously
appear in places scarred by reckless magic and feed on
the energy of living creatures to sustain their unnatural
existence.
Lash crawlers gather in small groups of five to ten in
caves and ruins, usually in places that have endured
bombardment from wild and chaotic magic.
LASH CRAWLER DIFFICULTY 1
Size 1/4 frightening monster
Perception 20 (+10); truesight
Defense 13; Health 5; Insanity —; Corruption —
Strength 8 (–2), Agility 13 (+3), Intellect 8 (–2), Will 11 (+1)
Speed 12; climber
ATTACK OPTIONS
Tendril (melee) +3 (1)
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Warping Gaze The lash crawler makes a Will attack roll
against the Agility of one target creature it can see
within medium range of it. On a success, the target takes
1d6 damage and moves 1 yard in a direction the crawler
chooses.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Extract Eye The lash crawler uses an action or a triggered
action on its turn to remove an eye from one target
defenseless creature within its reach. At the end of the
round, the eye becomes a new lash crawler.
Spring Away When a creature the lash crawler can see
gets a failure on an attack roll against the lash crawler’s
Defense or Agility, the lash crawler can use a triggered
action to retreat.

originalText:
Leshy
The leshy walk the primeval forests, tending to the trees
and encouraging saplings to grow tall and strong. Leshy
dislike humans for their carelessness but despise orcs and
other filthy creatures that wantonly burn and destroy. Leshy
sometimes join forces with druids against a common enemy.
A leshy looks like a tree of any species, though oak is
most common. A leshy that stands still is indistinguishable
from a normal tree and might hold this position for
decades. When it does move, the lower trunk splits into
long legs. The leshy’s face peers out from the center of its
trunk, and it can bend its branches to use as arms.
A leshy typically speaks the Common Tongue and Elvish,
and it can communicate with any plant within 100 yards of it.
LESHY DIFFICULTY 250
Size 3 plant
Perception 15 (+5); shadowsight
Defense 20; Health 110; Insanity 0; Corruption 0
Strength 17 (+7), Agility 10 (+0), Intellect 11 (+1), Will 15 (+5)
Speed 10

stunned; a living leshy cannot be moved against its will

originalText:
Living Tar
Living tar is a mobile slick of black slime that creeps
toward anything it detects with its weird senses. It
gathers up its body into pseudopods with which it
smashes prey, then absorbs their vital fluids.
Some believe that living tar is the essence of slain demons
trapped in the mortal world.

---

Bestiary
LIVING TAR DIFFICULTY 100
Size 3 frightening ooze
Perception 15 (+5); sightless
Defense 14; Health 80; Insanity —; Corruption —
Strength 14 (+4), Agility 8 (–2), Intellect 5 (–5), Will 15 (+5)
Speed 6; climber, swimmer
Immune damage from cold; blinded, charmed, dazed,
diseased, frightened, grabbed, poisoned, prone, stunned,
and any effect that would change the living tar’s shape
Corrosive Body A living tar takes half damage from
weapons.
When a living tar takes damage from a metal or
wooden weapon that is not magical, the weapon
becomes partly dissolved, or is destroyed if already
partly dissolved. A creature that attacks with a partly
dissolved weapon makes the attack roll with 1 bane.
Division When a living tar takes damage from lightning or
a weapon and the damage does not incapacitate it, it
divides. A second tar moves out from the original’s space
into an open space within 1 yard of it. The Size of each
tar drops by 1, and the new tars each have Health equal
to half of the original. Each tar has half the damage total
of the original before it divided.
		 A living tar cannot divide if it is smaller than Size 1.
Amorphous A living tar can squeeze through openings
wide enough to permit the passage of water, and it can
move through spaces occupied by other creatures.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Pseudopod (melee) +4 with 2 boons (5d6 plus Dissolve
Armor)
Dissolve Armor If the target is a creature that is made
of metal or that is wearing medium or heavy armor, it
takes a -1 penalty to its Defense. If this penalty reduces
the Defense provided by the armor to 10, the armor is
destroyed. If this penalty reduces a metallic creature’s
Defense to 10, the creature becomes incapacitated.
END OF THE ROUND
Dissolve Metal and Wood The living tar dissolves 2 inches
of wood or 1 inch of metal in contact with it.
