container.coverage: PDF pp. 3–5. [CRIATURA] [REGRA]

originalText:
Horned Champion
Every warrior who becomes a horned champion undergoes
the Rite of Becoming. The candidate strips off all clothing,
dons a blindfold, and then marches off into the deepest
woods. At some point later, the Horned King finds them. If
he deems them worthy, the god has his way with them. If
not, they never return. Bloodied, bruised, weakened, and
filled to the brim with divine seed, they transform to adopt
their god’s likeness.
All horned champions have sharp antlers growing from
their foreheads, eyes that shine with green light, and whorls
in their skin. They say nothing as the god fills their minds
with strange visions of being wild animals hunting prey in
the woods. All distraction falls away in battle, though. They
fight with singular focus to kill their opponents.
HORNED CHAMPION DIFFICULTY 25
Perception 12 (+2)
Defense 13 (hides), Health 60, Insanity 6, Corruption 2
Strength 13 (+3), Agility 11 (+1), Intellect 10 (+0), Will 13 (+3)
Descriptor Human, Size 1, Speed 12
Languages Western Dialect, animal tongues
Immune frightened
Blood Frenzy When the horned champion takes damage,
they make attack rolls with 1 boon and their attacks deal
1d6 extra damage until the end of their next turn.
Swift and Sudden Moves At the start of the horned
champion’s turn, roll a d6. On a 6, they teleport to an
empty space within 12 yards and make attack rolls with 1
boon until the start of their next turn.
Melee Attack—Axe Strength (+3) with 1 boon (2d6 + 1)
Strike Again (Attack) When the horned champion deals 9
damage or more with an attack, they can use a triggered
action to attack.

container.section: ## 64. Wild Beasts — adversários & Shadow effects
container.coverage: PDF pp. 3–5. [CRIATURA] [REGRA]

originalText:
Campaign
Their single-minded purpose and their zeal in carrying
out their mission make the Wild Beasts a singular threat to
the stability of the Northern Reach. Unlike the beastmen
horde, Wild Beasts have sufficient intelligence to outwit
defenders and the resolve to keep fighting, even after
suffering disastrous setbacks. Their warped interpretation
of the Horned King risks transforming the god into
something monstrous and evil.
The following entries provide you with a broad-strokes
story so you can create adventures that feature the cult
as the primary antagonist. In addition, each tier includes
a Shadow of the Demon Lord entry to show how the
corruption burgeons to make it easier for the Hunger in the
Void to enter this world and consume it.
The Gathering Beasts
(Novice)
One by one, villages and hamlets all across the western
hinterlands go dark as the Wild Beasts invade. The
barbarians punch through walls, chop up the defenders,
and take as prisoners the rest. Captured people can join the
Wild Beasts. Any potential convert must demonstrate their
worth and faith by killing one of their neighbors. The rest
end up marched east or butchered.

container.section: ## 64. Wild Beasts — adversários & Shadow effects
container.coverage: PDF pp. 3–5. [CRIATURA] [REGRA]

originalText:
Shadow of the Demon Lord: All natural and ordinary
animals become aggressive. Even domesticated animals
turn on their keepers. Cattle stampede to trample
handlers, while horses buck off riders and kick them
while they’re down. Pets run off, some even attacking
their owners before vanishing.

---

Horned Prince (Expert)
One of the horned champions declares himself the true son
of the Horned King, the god clad in mortal flesh. Dubbed
the Horned Prince, he takes control over the cult by killing
several priests, specifically those who doubt his divinity.
The survivors fall into line and the host’s numbers swell
with beastmen welcomed into their ranks. The Wild Beasts,
emboldened by their new leader, push into settled lands.
A force camps around Crossings to lay siege, while the rest
spread through the surrounding lands. The Wild Beasts no
longer take prisoners; they kill everyone.

container.coverage: PDF pp. 3–5. [CRIATURA] [REGRA]

originalText:
Shadow of the Demon Lord: Ordinary people’s patience
and tolerance drain out of them until they become bitter
and angry. Friendships fail, families break apart, violent
crime erupts just about everywhere. People who give
in to their aggressive tendencies discover patches of fur
sprouting from their bodies, and their facial features
become bestial.
A Monstrous God (Master)
The Wild Beasts overrun the Northern Reach, from the
Firepeaks to the shores of the Auroral Ocean. They have
become a horde comprising human and monstrous
members. The host pours through the Shadow Pass
enabling travel to the south and invades the Empire,
already vulnerable from its own internecine struggles.
As mighty as the horde has become, though, it shows
weakness. Warriors removed from the Horned Prince lose
some of their aggressiveness and can be easily confused.
Killing the Horned Prince might cause the whole host to
fall apart.

originalText:
Troglodyte
The rank and file members of the troglodyte band,
these wretched peoples thrive on sowing chaos, causing
pain, and their own suffering. They gather in large
mobs, using brute force to overwhelm their enemies.
TROGLODYTE DIFFICULTY 10
Size 1 frightening troglodyte
Perception 12 (+2); darksight
Defense 10; Health 20; Insanity —; Corruption 3
Strength 13 (+3), Agility 10 (+0), Intellect 8 (–2), Will 9 (–1)
Speed 12
Immune gaining Insanity; frightened
Strength from Pain While injured, the troglodyte makes
attack rolls with 1 boon and its weapon attacks deal 1d6
extra damage.
Sunlight Weakness A troglodyte is impaired while in areas
lit by sunlight.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Pick (melee) +3 with 1 boon (1d6 + 2)
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Hide in Shadows The troglodyte can attempt to hide when
it is at least partially obscured by shadows, even if it’s
being observed.

container.section: ## 65. Wretched and Unclean — troglodyte adversaries
container.coverage: PDF pp. 3–6. [CRIATURA]

originalText:
God-Killer
Veteran troglodyte warriors can earn higher standing
among their tribes by finding a mortal priest and
dragging him into the darkness. There, the troglodyte
must torture the priest until he renounces his faith, at
which point the troglodyte rips out the priest’s tongue,
anus, and heart. After devouring all three in front of
the gathered host, the troglodyte becomes a god-killer.
God-killers wear the broken holy signs and icons of
the religions they have despoiled on chains around
their necks. They always seek out new priests to slay,
hooting when they cut them down.

---

GOD-KILLER DIFFICULTY 50
Size 1 frightening troglodyte
Perception 13 (+3); darksight
Defense 12; Health 40; Insanity —; Corruption 6
Strength 14 (+4), Agility 12 (+2), Intellect 9 (–1), Will 10 (+0)
Speed 12
Immune gaining Insanity; frightened
Kill the Weak A god-killer makes attack rolls with 1 boon
against frightened targets.
Strength from Pain While injured, the troglodyte makes
attack rolls with 1 boon and its weapon attacks deal 1d6
extra damage.
Sunlight Weakness A troglodyte is impaired while in areas
lit by sunlight.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Greatsword (melee) +4 with 2 boons (3d6)
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Double Attack The god-killer attacks twice with its
greatsword.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Hide in Shadows The troglodyte can attempt to hide when
it is at least partially obscured by shadows, even if it’s
being observed.
Frightful Howl The god-killer shrieks. Each creature that
is not a troglodyte within 20 yards that can hear it must
get a success on a Will challenge roll with 1 bane or
become frightened for 1 minute.

originalText:
Slave of Ashrakal
The debased cult devoted to the Witch-King’s memory
thrives in the cloying darkness of the troglodytes’
caves. Many give their lives to worship and service of
their ancient master, proving their loyalty by cutting
off or out their genitals and eating them to show their
devotion to their god and master.
Slaves forgo clothing to show the ruin of their loins
as proof of their dedication. They carve their bodies
with serpentine shapes, inking the wounds with coal
dust to represent the black serpents released from the
Witch-King’s body at the moment of his death.
SLAVE OF ASHRAKAL DIFFICULTY 10
Size 1 frightening troglodyte
Perception 15 (+5); darksight
Defense 9; Health 24; Insanity —; Corruption 4
Strength 12 (+2), Agility 9 (–1), Intellect 11 (+1), Will 10 (+0)
Speed 12
Immune gaining Insanity; frightened
Strength from Pain While injured, the troglodyte makes
attack rolls with 1 boon and its weapon attacks deal 1d6
extra damage.
Sunlight Weakness A troglodyte is impaired while in areas
lit by sunlight.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Claws and Teeth (melee) +2 (1d3)
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Hide in Shadows The troglodyte can attempt to hide when
it is at least partially obscured by shadows, even if it’s
being observed.
Wail for the Master The slave uses an action to loose an
otherworldly scream. Each creature in a 3-yard cone
originating from a point in the slave’s space must make a
Will challenge roll with 1 bane. On a failure, the creature
gains 1d3 Insanity. Once the slave uses Wail for the
Master, it cannot do so again until it completes a rest.
MAGIC
Power 1
Divination epiphany (2), foretell (1)
Forbidden black tongue (2), obedience (1)
Shadow nightfall blade (2), darkness (1)

container.section: ## 65. Wretched and Unclean — troglodyte adversaries
container.coverage: PDF pp. 3–6. [CRIATURA]

originalText:
Pale Bride
The raven-haired pale brides pledge themselves to
their tribe’s abomination and bear his children. In
tribes led by female abominations, pale brides are
called pale consorts instead, but are otherwise the
same. Sleek of body and frightfully quick, they dance
across the battlefield, slashing with their whips and
knives, leaving crimson stripes on their victims’
bodies. Pale brides laugh as they torment their prey,
licking the blood from their fingers and touching
themselves with excitement whenever their enemies
scream.
PALE BRIDE DIFFICULTY 50
Size 1 frightening troglodyte
Perception 14 (+4); darksight
Defense 14; Health 30; Insanity —; Corruption 6
Strength 10 (+0), Agility 14 (+4), Intellect 10 (+0), Will 11 (+1)
Speed 12
Immune gaining Insanity; frightened
Strength from Pain While injured, the troglodyte makes
attack rolls with 1 boon and its weapon attacks deal 1d6
extra damage.
Sunlight Weakness A troglodyte is impaired while in areas
lit by sunlight.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Long Knife (melee) +4 with 3 boons (2d6)
Whip (melee; reach 2) +4 with 3 boons (1d3 plus 1d6 plus
Exquisite Agony)
Exquisite Agony A living creature of flesh and blood must
make a Will challenge roll with 2 banes. On a success,
the target creature becomes immune to this pale bride’s
Exquisite Agony until the target completes a rest. On
a failure, the target gains 1d6 Insanity. While the target
is frightened from gaining Insanity in this way, it is
charmed.
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Dancing Attack If the pale bride is not grabbed,
immobilized, or slowed, she attacks with her long knife
and whip. The bride can move 1 yard between each
attack without triggering a free attack.
Obey Me The pale bride uses an action, or a triggered
action on her turn, to make a Will attack roll with 1 boon
against the Will of one charmed creature within short
range. If the bride used a triggered action, she makes the
roll with 1 bane. On a success, the target is compelled for
1 round.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Hide in Shadows The troglodyte can attempt to hide when
it is at least partially obscured by shadows, even if it’s
being observed.

---

Dark Speaker
The dark speakers keep the magical lore handed
down from the warlocks of old. While they have lost
much knowledge from the ancient times, they have
retained enough to be dangerous. As part of their
initiation, dark speakers must carve out their eyes
with sharp rocks and mutilate the skin around them.
Then, if found worthy by their master, a grisly red eye
opens in the center of their foreheads. Dark speakers
wear tattered black cloaks and carve arcane symbols
into their skin.

container.coverage: PDF pp. 3–6. [CRIATURA]

originalText:
Abomination
The strong and depraved rule troglodyte
communities. Called abominations, these hideous
troglodytes might be male or female and have first
choice of mates, making their favorites pale brides
(or consorts). Abominations feed their appetites
and subjugate the tribe members and prisoners to
whatever debased thing they can conceive.
Abominations almost hum with the corruption
in their souls and display a variety of bizarre and
appalling marks of darkness. They wear these signs
with pride, leaking foul milk from their nipples,
clutching the baby faces festooning their bellies,
or savagely beating themselves in anticipation of
the coming battle. Horns, claws, sharpened teeth,
strange writings under the skin, calcified fetuses
dangling from blackened umbilical cords hanging
from between their legs are but a few of the possible
manifestations of their particular brand of evil.

---

ABOMINATION DIFFICULTY 100
Size 1 horrifying troglodyte
Perception 13 (+3); darksight
Defense 11; Health 100; Insanity —; Corruption 10
Strength 16 (+6), Agility 11 (+1), Intellect 9 (–1), Will 12 (+2)
Speed 12
Immune gaining Insanity; frightened
Lord of Darkness Each troglodyte friendly to the
abomination and within short range of it makes attack
rolls with 1 boon and deals 1d6 extra damage on its
attacks.
Strength from Pain While injured, the troglodyte makes
attack rolls with 1 boon and its weapon attacks deal
1d6 extra damage.
Sunlight Weakness A troglodyte is impaired while in areas
lit by sunlight.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Axe (melee) +6 with 2 boons (3d6)
Harpoon (medium range) +6 with 1 boon (3d6 plus Tethered)
Tethered A creature with a physical body becomes
tethered. While tethered, the creature cannot move
away from the abomination. If the abomination would
move away from the tethered creature, it must either
drop the line or make a Strength attack roll with 1 boon
against the target’s Strength, dragging the target with
it when it moves on a success. An abomination can
have just one creature tethered at a time. A tethered
creature can remove the affliction by using an action to
rip the harpoon free, which deals 1d6 extra damage to
that creature.
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Double Attack The abomination attacks twice with its axe.
Or, the abomination uses Reel In and then attacks with
its axe.
Reel In The abomination makes a Strength attack roll
with 1 boon against the Strength of one creature it has
tethered. If the target is larger than the abomination,
it makes the roll with 1 bane. On a success, the target
takes 1d6 damage and moves up to 6 yards toward the
abomination.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Hide in Shadows The troglodyte can attempt to hide when
it is at least partially obscured by shadows, even if it’s
being observed.
END OF THE ROUND
Feed the Corruption The abomination radiates a field
of corruption. Any creature within short range that is
not a troglodyte and has 1 Corruption or more must
make a Will challenge roll with 3 banes. On a success, a
creature becomes immune to this abomination’s Feed
the Corruption until the creature completes a rest. On
a failure, the creature gains 1 Corruption and becomes
dazed for 1 round.

container.coverage: PDF pp. 3–6. [CRIATURA]

originalText:
Serpent of the Witch-King
The Serpents of the Witch-King are the undead
servants of Ashrakal who have managed to survive the
long centuries by drinking the life force from living
things, such as those sacrificed to them by bands of
troglodyte Witch-King worshippers. Serpents of the
Witch-King do not belong in this world. They walk
through the air, as if the very ground below them
cannot bear their touch. Scraps of black clothing
flutter around the emaciated wreckage of their ancient
flesh. Their red eyes burn with the fires of Hell and
their long, sharp claws curl around slender fingers.
SERPENT OF THE WITCH-KING DIFFICULTY 500
Size 1 horrifying undead
Perception 19 (+9); darksight
Defense 14; Health 125; Insanity —; Corruption 13
Strength 15 (+5), Agility 14 (+4), Intellect 15 (+5), Will 12 (+2)
Speed 12; flier
Immune damage from cold, disease, or poison; gaining
Insanity; asleep, dazed, diseased, fatigued, frightened,
poisoned, stunned
Abhorrent to Urth A serpent of Ashrakal always walks
3 inches above the ground and never takes damage
from landing after a fall.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Claws (melee) +5 with 3 boons (4d6)
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Drink Life Inky darkness streaks toward a creature within
medium range. The serpent makes an Intellect attack roll
with 1 boon against the target’s Agility. On a success, the
beam strikes the target and raises it up until it stands
3 yards above the ground. The target is stunned for as
long as the Serpent concentrates. Each time the Serpent
uses an action to concentrate on this effect, the target
takes a cumulative –2d6 penalty to its Health. If the
accumulated penalty drops the target’s Health to 0, it
dies and its body crumbles to ash. If the Serpent takes
any damage while concentrating on this effect, the
damage breaks its concentration and ends the effect.
Once a Serpent uses this action, it must wait at least one
minute before it can do so again.
Tears of the Witch-King The Serpent flicks black droplets
at up to five creatures within medium range. A target
must get a success on an Agility challenge roll with 1
bane or be struck by the droplet. A creature struck by
the droplet gains 1d6 Insanity and becomes compelled
for as long as it is frightened from gaining Insanity in this
way. Once the Serpent uses this action, it cannot do so
until it completes a rest.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Shadow Wards The Serpent creates five shadow wards.
Whenever a creature within short range damages the
Serpent, the Serpent can use a triggered action to
dismiss one of the wards, causing a clot of shadow to fly
toward the triggering creature. The triggering creature
must get a success on an Agility challenge roll with 1
bane or become blinded for 1 hour.
MAGIC
Power 5
Death (Demon Lord’s Companion) killing touch (6), life
drain (3), decay (2), feast of souls (2), death fog (1),
stop heart (1)
Forbidden black tongue (6), hateful defecation (3),
ravenous maggots (2), desire’s end (2), soul exchange (1),
horrid joining (1)
END OF THE ROUND
Burned by Sunlight The Serpent takes 2d6 damage if it is
in an area lit by sunlight.

container.coverage: PDF pp. 2–3. [REGRA] [DEPENDÊNCIA OMITIDA]

originalText:
Eudaemonic Bonds
Anyone who displays the proper commitment to one of the
cardinal virtues might gain attention from an eudaemon,
but they offer no explanation for why they might single out
some but not others. One person could choose the good
instead of the tempting wrong and feel the eudaemon come
upon them, but another who delivers justice to a villain of
the highest order feels little more than the accomplishment
of a job well done.
Your character, however, stands apart from others of
your kind. Destiny steers your course, or you have a special
talent, or you just have a bit more luck than other folks
have. Provided you meet the requirements listed under the
eudaemons described below, you can apply the benefits
to your character. Note, though, that binding with a
eudaemon comes with some risk. The eudaemons aid those
who embody their virtues, but if their chosen fall short, the
eudaemons deliver swift and terrible punishment.
If you bond with an eudaemon, you will never be alone
again. You feel the entity around you—watching, weighing
your actions, judging you. The eudaemon has no body and
makes no sound, but you know they are always present.
Seeing symbols of the virtue the eudaemon represents
could reflect the actions of the entity, or it might just be
your mind playing tricks, showing you what you expect
to see. If ever you disappoint your eudaemon, you feel
their wrath coursing through your body. Unless you make
amends, you might lose them forever.

2

container.coverage: PDF pp. 2–4. [REGRA] [EQUIPAMENTO] [CRIATURA]

originalText:
Parasites

The parasites found below use the same format and
mechanical concepts as the diseases introduced in
Fever Dreams. A parasite’s entry tells you something
about it, how one becomes a host, the symptoms
of infection, and any known cures. The mechanics
follow.
Once a creature becomes infected with a parasite,
the infestation marks its progression through a
series of worsening stages that culminate in some
permanent impairment or death. At specific intervals
described in the recovery section, the afflicted
creature makes challenge rolls to resist the parasites.
The result of the roll causes the infection’s effect to
move up to a higher stage or down to a lower stage.
This continues until the infection reaches its final
stage or the creature becomes cured through a series
of successful rolls or from acquiring the actual cure.

Black Moth Larvae

“Black” fails to capture just how dark are the wings
of the black moths. These tiny insects seem to drink
in the light, and look like fluttering holes in reality.
Although small, delicate, fragile even, the black
moths pose terrible danger to other creatures and
infestations have been known to wipe out entire
communities.
Black moths lay their eggs in the bodies of living
creatures, typically when such creatures are asleep,
choosing places with access to the warm interior of
the body such as the nostrils, ear canals, or open
mouth. A moth can lay dozens of eggs, attaching
each to the walls with an adhesive made from its
reproductive juices, and then flutters off to die. Several
days later, the moth eggs hatch and the larvae eat
their way free from the host.
Purge Broth Finding and manually removing
the eggs inside a host’s body before they hatch
proves a fruitless exercise; the eggs are simply too
small and hide in places normally out of reach.
Apothecaries, especially those in rural areas, have
concocted a cure called purge broth, though people
who sample its foul flavor report the cure is as bad as
the infestation. Made from rotting stinkweed leaves,
powdered gallstones, and a number of other unsavory
substances (1 ss worth of exotic materials), the potion
must be consumed in a single swallow for maximum
effectiveness. The drinker experiences a strange
flushing, almost as if it was burning from inside
out. This flushing causes the larvae to exit the body
through the fastest available route, which causes the
drinker to take 1d6 + 3 damage as wriggling maggotlike things spill out in a bloody wash from all of its
orifices.

originalText:
Black Moth Larvae Effects
Infection If a creature completes a rest in an outdoor
wilderness environment in an area containing at least
one black moth, the creature must, 1d3 + 1 days later,
make a Strength challenge roll with 1 bane. On a failure,
the creature suffers the effects of stage 1 infection.
While infected, the creature is diseased and, each time
it completes a rest, must make a Strength challenge roll
with an additional 1 bane, plus any banes imposed by the
stage. Find the results of the roll below.
• Success, 20 or higher Reduce the infection stage by one.
• Success No change.
• Failure Increase the infection stage by one.
• Failure, 0 or lower Increase the infection stage by two.
Stage 0 The creature recovers from the black moth larvae
infection and becomes immune to it for 24 hours.
Stage 1 The creature has a 1d6 penalty to its Health and
makes Strength attack rolls and challenge rolls with 1
bane.
Stage 2 The creature has a 2d6 penalty to its Health and
makes Strength attack rolls and challenge rolls with 2
banes.
Stage 3 The creature has a 3d6 penalty to its Health and
makes Strength attack rolls and challenge rolls with 3
banes.
Stage 4 The creature takes damage equal to its Health
and releases from its body a cloud of black moths that
partially obscure the air within short range of the dead
creature for 1d6 rounds before dispersing.
Aftereffects The creature makes Strength attack rolls and
challenge rolls with 1 bane for 1d6 days.

originalText:
Bloat Worms
Many parasites invade hosts through the food
they eat. Meat, in particular, can carry all kinds of
terrifying parasites, if it’s not properly cooked. Bloat
worms are one such parasite that breeds in spoiled
meat, though how they come to be there is anyone’s
guess. Creatures who consume the rancid flesh take in
the worms, which then spread throughout the host’s
body with alarming speed and to awful effect.
Bloat worms release gas as they feed on their hosts,
creating slowly expanding bubbles that eventually
push out the skin to form hardened bulges. A minor
infection might result in a few weirdly discolored
raised areas on the body, while the more severe
infections can make the hosts unrecognizable
monsters. If the host dies, the pent-up gas releases
with explosive force to blow apart the body in a
shower of blood, bones, and flapping skin.
Alcohol Binge The best way to rid oneself of bloat
worms is to drink several gallons of alcohol over a
period of seven days.
The change in blood
chemistry makes the
body inhospitable to
the bloat worms and,
at the end of the seventh
day, they evacuate in
a forceful spray from
the host’s bowels (as
the hateful defecation
Forbidden spell).

--- PDF p. 3 ---

originalText:
Intellect Eater

The dreaded intellect eater has been a scourge in
recent days and victims of these parasites have been
turning up in the Confederacy’s lands, especially in
the client villages and towns who support the larger
cities. Intellect eaters infest sewers and enter their
victims’ bodies through the openings of their sexual
organs and conceal their entry with the anesthetizing
slime their thin bodies exude.
Once inside the host, the eater coils around its
victim’s spine, where it remains dormant for a full year,
feeding on the host’s spinal fluid, while it grows ever
larger. When it reaches adulthood, the worm chews a
hole out from the base of its host’s throat. Fully sentient,
when the intellect eater partly emerges from the host, it
takes control of the host’s body and can communicate
using the host’s mouth and vocal cords.

Intellect Eater Effects
Infection A creature that moves through a fluid infested
with intellect eaters, such as in a pit underneath an
outhouse or a city sewer might become infected by
the parasite. Roll a d6. On a 6, the parasite invades the
host’s body by way of its genitals. While infected, the
host creature makes Agility attack rolls and challenge
rolls with 1 bane and grants 1 boon on attack rolls made
against its Agility. One year after infection, the worm
reaches maturity with the following effects.
A mature intellect eater shares control of the host
body until the host body dies, which kills the parasite as
well. The eater uses the following statistics.

INTELLECT EATER

DIFFICULTY 5

Size 1/8 horrifying monster
Perception 15 (+5); darksight
Defense *; Health *; Insanity 0; Corruption 4
Strength 5 (–5), Agility 5 (–5), Intellect 12 (+2), Will 13 (+3)
Speed 2
Shared Defense and Health The intellect eater uses the
host’s Defense and Health scores. The intellect eater can
also use the host’s Strength and Agility in place of its
own for as long as it resides in the host’s body.

Immune dazed, stunned
Parasite The intellect eater resides inside of its host’s body.
If the host dies, so too does the intellect eater. The eater
can use an action once per round, taking its turn when
its host does. The parasite uses its host’s body to resolve
the use of its action.

Mind Fire
It takes just one of these amorphous microorganisms
entering the body for it to wreak havoc. The
organism moves through its host along its blood
stream until it takes root in the brain, where it
remains, eating away at the gray matter until it is so
full of holes the victim dies. The infection causes
derangement, erratic behavior, and violent outbursts.
Victims of mind fire run a low fever and blood pools
in the sclera of their eyes.
Surgery The organism grows larger as it feeds on
its victim’s brain and its wet, slippery, formless body
fills in the holes that it creates. A victim at Stage 3
or higher might be rescued from the disease as the
parasite is of a size large enough to be surgically
extracted. A healer or surgeon can make the attempt,
which requires sawing away a portion of the skull
and rooting around inside the brain to reveal the
creature from the brain tissue its body has replaced.
Then, it’s just a matter of tongs and a firm grip to
remove it.
A creature who undergoes this surgery takes a
permanent 1d3 penalty to its Intellect score and
gains 1d6 Insanity, which cannot be reduced by
any means.

Mind Fire Effects
Infection The next time a creature who consumes
contaminated water or food completes a rest, the
creature must make a Strength challenge roll with 2 banes.
On a failure, the creature suffers the effects of stage
1 infection. While infected, the creature is diseased
and, each time it completes a rest, must make another
Strength challenge roll with 2 banes. Find the results of
the roll below.
• Success, 20 or higher Reduce the infection stage by one.
• Success No change.
• Failure Increase the infection stage by one.
• Failure, 0 or lower Increase the infection stage by two.
Stage 0 The creature recovers from mind fire and becomes
immune to it for 24 hours.
Stage 1 The creature makes Will challenge rolls with 2 banes.
Stage 2 As stage 1, and the creature gains 1d6 Insanity.
If the creature becomes subject to madness, do not roll
on the Madness table. Instead, the creature becomes
subject to Violence.
Stage 3 As stage 1, and the creature gains 2d6 Insanity.
If the creature becomes subject to madness, do not roll
on the Madness table. Instead, the creature becomes
subject to Violence and rolls twice, using the lower
result, to end the madness effect.
Stage 4 The creature takes damage equal to its Health
and a mind fire slime slithers out from its nostrils. The
creature is hostile to all creatures and takes the next
available turn to attack the creature nearest to it.
Aftereffects The creature’s maximum amount of Insanity
is permanently reduced by 2.

--- PDF p. 4 ---

Defense *; Health *; Insanity 0; Corruption 4
Strength 5 (–5), Agility 5 (–5), Intellect 12 (+2), Will 13 (+3)
Speed 2
Shared Defense and Health The intellect eater uses the
host’s Defense and Health scores. The intellect eater can
also use the host’s Strength and Agility in place of its
own for as long as it resides in the host’s body.

Immune dazed, stunned
Parasite The intellect eater resides inside of its host’s body.
If the host dies, so too does the intellect eater. The eater
can use an action once per round, taking its turn when
its host does. The parasite uses its host’s body to resolve
the use of its action.

Mind Fire
It takes just one of these amorphous microorganisms
entering the body for it to wreak havoc. The
organism moves through its host along its blood
stream until it takes root in the brain, where it
remains, eating away at the gray matter until it is so
full of holes the victim dies. The infection causes
derangement, erratic behavior, and violent outbursts.
Victims of mind fire run a low fever and blood pools
in the sclera of their eyes.
Surgery The organism grows larger as it feeds on
its victim’s brain and its wet, slippery, formless body
fills in the holes that it creates. A victim at Stage 3
or higher might be rescued from the disease as the
parasite is of a size large enough to be surgically
extracted. A healer or surgeon can make the attempt,
which requires sawing away a portion of the skull
and rooting around inside the brain to reveal the
creature from the brain tissue its body has replaced.
Then, it’s just a matter of tongs and a firm grip to
remove it.
A creature who undergoes this surgery takes a
permanent 1d3 penalty to its Intellect score and
gains 1d6 Insanity, which cannot be reduced by
any means.

Mind Fire Effects
Infection The next time a creature who consumes
contaminated water or food completes a rest, the
creature must make a Strength challenge roll with 2 banes.
On a failure, the creature suffers the effects of stage
1 infection. While infected, the creature is diseased
and, each time it completes a rest, must make another
Strength challenge roll with 2 banes. Find the results of
the roll below.
• Success, 20 or higher Reduce the infection stage by one.
• Success No change.
• Failure Increase the infection stage by one.
• Failure, 0 or lower Increase the infection stage by two.
Stage 0 The creature recovers from mind fire and becomes
immune to it for 24 hours.
Stage 1 The creature makes Will challenge rolls with 2 banes.
Stage 2 As stage 1, and the creature gains 1d6 Insanity.
If the creature becomes subject to madness, do not roll
on the Madness table. Instead, the creature becomes
subject to Violence.
Stage 3 As stage 1, and the creature gains 2d6 Insanity.
If the creature becomes subject to madness, do not roll
on the Madness table. Instead, the creature becomes
subject to Violence and rolls twice, using the lower
result, to end the madness effect.
Stage 4 The creature takes damage equal to its Health
and a mind fire slime slithers out from its nostrils. The
creature is hostile to all creatures and takes the next
available turn to attack the creature nearest to it.
Aftereffects The creature’s maximum amount of Insanity
is permanently reduced by 2.

--- PDF p. 4 ---

originalText:
MIND FIRE SLIME

DIFFICULTY 5

Size 1/2 frightening ooze
Perception 10 (+0); sightless
Defense 8; Health 33; Insanity —; Corruption 0
Strength 11 (+1), Agility 8 (–2), Intellect 5 (–5), Will 15 (+5)
Speed 6; climber, swimmer
Immune damage from disease; blinded, charmed, dazed,
diseased, frightened, grabbed, prone, stunned, and any
effect that would change its shape.
Infectious Any living creature of flesh and blood that
touches or is touched by the mind fire slime becomes
exposed to mind fire.
Confounding Thoughts The mind fire slime broadcasts
the thoughts of creatures whose brains it has devoured.
At the end of each round, each creature within short
range of the slime must succeed on a Will challenge roll
with 1 bane or gain 1 Insanity. A successful challenge roll
renders the creature immune to this slime’s confounding
thoughts until the creature completes a rest.

ATTACK OPTIONS
Pseudopod (melee) +1 with 3 boons (2d6)

Nerothian
Fungal Spores

Like the rot maiden, the nerothian fungus too has
a humanoid shape, but rather than attaining that
shape by growth, the form comes from the creature
victimized by its spores. Nerothian fungus thrives
when it grows in rotting meat, and from the inverted
caps that unfold all over the body waft millions
of spores drifting in the breeze and searching for
purchase on the body of a nearby creature.
So small are these motes that they can lodge in skin
pores and take root, tendrils spreading throughout the
body to control the host’s nervous system. After a few
days, the fungus makes its host into something like a
zombie, until the body finally gives out and dies.
Immolation Fire destroys the fungus’s spores
and thus the only real cure for this infestation is to
burn the victim alive or near enough that the spores
die while leaving the host creature a burned ruin.
A creature infected with the spores that becomes
incapacitated by damage from fire and at least half the
damage in its damage total comes from fire is cured of
the infection.

Nerothian Fungal Spores Effects
Infection A corpse of a creature that succumbed to the
spore infection emits spores that partially obscure a
sphere of space with a 5-yard radius centered on a
point in the corpse’s space. Any creature that enters the
area of spores becomes infected. A creature with fur
covering its body can roll a d20 and escapes infection
on a roll of 10 or higher. A creature infected in this way
suffers the stage 1 effects of the parasites 24 hours later.
Henceforth, whenever the infected creature completes a
rest, it must make a Strength challenge roll with 3 banes.
Find the results of the roll below.
• Success, 20 or higher Reduce the infection stage by one.
• Success No change.
• Failure Increase the infection stage by one.
• Failure, 0 or lower Increase the infection stage by two.
Stage 0 The creature recovers from the nerothian fungal
spores and becomes immune to it for 24 hours.
Stage 1 The creature is diseased.
Stage 2 As stage 1, but the creature is also impaired and
slowed.
Stage 3 As stage 2, but whenever the creature gets a
failure on an attack roll or challenge roll, the creature
becomes controlled by the GM for 1d3 rounds.
Stage 4 The creature becomes a fungal thrall of its Size
and stops making Strength challenge rolls to fight the
infection. The creature remains a fungal thrall until it dies.
Apply the following template to the creature.

FUNGAL THRALL

DIFFICULTY REDUCE BY ONE

fungus
Perception 10 (+0); sightless
Insanity —; Corruption —
Intellect —, Will —
Speed 6
Immune asleep, blinded, dazed, deafened, fatigued,
frightened, stunned
Fungal Control Unless attacked, in which case it defends
itself, the fungal thrall takes a fast turn each round and
moves its Speed in a randomly determined direction.
Infectious Spores When a creature that can reach the
fungal thrall deals damage to it with a melee weapon,
the attacking creature must succeed on an Intellect
challenge roll or become infected with the spores as
described above.

MAGIC
Power 0
The creature loses all traditions and spells.
Aftereffects When attacked by a fungus, the creature
grants the attacking creature 1 boon on its attack roll.

DIFFICULTY 10

Size 1 frightening monster (aquatic)
Perception 13 (+3); darksight
Defense 12; Health 40; Insanity 6, Corruption 4
Strength 11 (+1), Agility 10 (+0), Intellect 11 (+1), Will 12 (+2)

Amphibious A fallen priest can breathe while submerged in

Sleeper Awakens Before the fallen priest makes an attack roll

container.section: ## 70. Seekers of the Sleeping God — adversários, Astronomica e Shadow effects
container.coverage: PDF pp. 4–5. [CRIATURA] [EQUIPAMENTO] [REGRA] [DEPENDÊNCIA OMITIDA]

originalText:
Agents of the Sleeper
The cult depends on capable individuals to do the work
of finding the Astronomica, defending the priests and their
temples, and eliminating enemies. Like the priests, these
agents bear markings of their service, corruptions of
the flesh and mind that demonstrate their steady loss of
humanity.

AGENTS OF THE SLEEPER

DIFFICULTY 5

Size 1 monster
Perception 11 (+1)
Defense 14 (brigandine, small shield); Health 15; Insanity 4,
Corruption 2
Strength 12 (+2), Agility 10 (+0), Intellect 10 (+0), Will 11 (+1)
Speed 10
Gift of the Sleeping God Before the agent makes an attack
roll or challenge roll, they can use this trait to make the roll
with a number of boons equal to their Insanity. If the roll
results in a failure, the agent gains 1 Insanity and becomes
stunned until the end of their next turn.

ATTACK OPTIONS
Saber (melee) +2 with 1 boon (1d6 + 2)
Crab Claw (melee) +2 with 1 boon (1d6 plus grab)
Grab As part of the attack, the agent can attempt to
grab the target. The agent can maintain a grab using a
triggered action on their turn.

--- PDF p. 5 ---
The Astronomica
The Cult of the New God understood the peril the
Astronomica posed and thus moved to remove it from the
lands of the Empire. Dozens of incomplete copies, partially
transcribed from an authentic copy, went into the pyres,
as did several fabrications, books bearing the title but
filled with nonsense. The Cult managed to secure several
authentic, complete books and then burned them. One
copy, however, escaped their clutches: the original.
The Astromica’s size and bulk make concealing it difficult:
It weighs 30 pounds and measures 3 feet by 2 feet by 1
foot. Worse, anyone lugging it around feels as if some
liquid sloshes around inside, which makes it even more
cumbersome. Some kind of coral-like growth completely
covers the book, even the pages. A starfish is found on one
side. Twisting it to the right detaches it from the book’s
surface. Once free, a potential reader must place the
starfish over their face, at which point it becomes affixed
until removed. Removing it deals 1 damage as the starfish
grows quite comfortable and loses interest in independent
living. While the starfish is in place, the reader sees the
book open—no others do—to reveal a pool of water. Words
swim up in the pool and disappear when read. It takes 80
hours to read the book, and only by finishing it can one
gain its powers.
Dread Knowledge of the Sleeping God: You gain 1d3
Insanity, 3 Corruption, and you become cursed (as if by
a rank 7 spell). While cursed in this way, you become
impaired while you are not submerged in water.
Magical Secrets: You discover the Madness and Water
traditions if you have not discovered them already. If
you have, you learn a rank 0 spell from the tradition
instead. Details on the Madness tradition appear in
Occult Philosophy.
Awaken the Sleeping God: The book contains a ritual
to awaken the sleeping one. The ritual requires 100
gc worth of exotic ingredients, the participation of 8
people, and 24 hours of constant prayer and recitals
of the mystic words, all performed on the edge of
the Auroral Ocean. Upon finishing the ritual, each
participant takes 8d6 damage and gains Insanity equal
to their Will scores. Then, the seas froth as a demon
prince rises from the depths. (See The Hunger in the
Void, page 64, for rules.) The prince looks exactly like
the idol: a towering humanoid with a squid head and
a mass of writhing tentacles surrounding its beak. The
now awakened thing rampages across the countryside,
visiting death and destruction to everything in its path.

5

A Dark Tide Rises
The Seekers of the Sleeping God present a grave danger
to Rûl. They act to awaken their eldritch master, heedless
of the horrors doing so will unleash on the world. The
Sleeping God’s influence blinds them to the reality of
what their service will bring and to the ravages that
worshipping their master inflicts upon their flesh. You can
use the following campaign structure to create a series of
adventures featuring the cult. Each tier includes a Shadow
of the Demon Lord to describe the perilous conditions
brought on by the Hunger’s attention.

Stirrings in the Deep (Novice)
The orcs invade the Holy Kingdom. They butcher the
inhabitants, torture the priests, and sack the temples. A
strange group of people follow them, seemingly priests of
Oceanus. However the characters become involved, they
must contend with the priests who take some acolytes
prisoner and torture them for information concerning a
lost tome they call the Astronomica.
Shadow of the Demon Lord: Gray-green clouds blot out
the skies and remain. Sometimes, they swirl around.
One can see emerald lightning reach down to scorch the
earth. It rains two days out of every three.

Seaward Shenanigans (Expert)
After a merchant ship loaded with medical supplies never
reaches Freeport, the authorities hire the player characters
to find it and recover what they can. During the voyage, the
characters encounter storms, a kraken attack, and devotees
of a bizarre god peering into the deep to find their sleeping
master. The characters learn that the cultists attack ships
and take them to widen the range of their search.
Shadow of the Demon Lord: It now rains every day and
flooding becomes a problem. Worse, the raindrops
contain some slimy mucus that taints water. People who
drink the tainted water gain fishy mutations after 1d3
days.

The Dread Ritual (Master)
The cultists recover the Astronomica and locate the Sleeping
One. They gather to perform the ritual on a ship when
Tarterus hides from the night sky, and all the planets align
with Urth in a row. The characters learn about the attempt
and have 24 hours to stop the ritual before it finishes. The
group must track down the ship, deal with the various
guardians in their path, and thwart Kristane and the
demons he summons, or all is lost.
Shadow of the Demon Lord: The rains become
downpours. Sea levels rise, and most coastal cities
and settlements drown. Worse, mutated people run
amok through the countryside, screeching and hooting
prayers to the Sleeper.

container.section: ## 71. Frayed Ends — quirks opcionais
container.coverage: PDF pp. 1–4. [OPCIONAL] [REGRA]

originalText:
Frayed Ends offers a new way to show the cost of gaining
Insanity in Shadow of the Demon Lord. Normally, player
characters can rid themselves of Insanity by gaining quirks,
odd, compulsive behaviors that sometimes reflect the sources
of Insanity characters acquire. This supplement goes beyond
the rules in Shadow and the Unhinge the Mind Poisoned Pages
expansion by presenting six tables of quirks you can use to
relieve your mind of the madness you have endured. Rather
than working with the GM to determine your quirk, whenever
you would gain a quirk, roll a d6 and find the numbered table
matching the number you rolled. Then, roll a d20 to find the
quirk you gain.
Quirks acquired from these tables might be personality
disorders, delusions, or strange behaviors that manifest
under specific situations. To preserve the game’s grim
atmosphere, it’s important to include quirks gained when
roleplaying. In doing so, you demonstrate both the fragility
of the mortal mind as well as the horrid experiences you have
endured so far. As with all Poisoned Pages additions, the rules
in this booklet are entirely optional. Before introducing them
into your games, be sure to discuss them with your players
and Game Master to ensure all are interested in heightening
the tension at the table.

evidence.heading: ## 71. Frayed Ends — quirks opcionais / Unassigned introduction
evidence.excerpt:
Frayed Ends offers a new way to show the cost of gaining
Insanity in Shadow of the Demon Lord. Normally, player
characters can rid themselves of Insanity by gaining quirks,
odd, compulsive behaviors that sometimes reflect the sources
of Insanity characters acquire. This supplement goes beyond
the rules in Shadow and the Unhinge the Mind Poisoned Pages
expansion by presenting six tables of quirks you can use to
relieve your mind of the madness you have endured. Rather
than working with the GM to determine your quirk, whenever
you would gain a quirk, roll a d6 and find the numbered table
matching the number you rolled. Then, roll a d20 to find the
quirk you gain.
Quirks acquired from these tables might be personality
disorders, delusions, or strange behaviors that manifest
under specific situations. To preserve the game’s grim
atmosphere, it’s important to include quirks gained when
roleplaying. In doing so, you demonstrate both the fragility
of the mortal mind as well as the horrid experiences you have
endured so far. As with all Poisoned Pages additions, the rules
in this booklet are entirely optional. Before introducing them
into your games, be sure to discuss them with your players
and Game Master to ensure all are interested in heightening
the tension at the table.

~Credits~

originalText:
Table 1: Quirks
d20

d20

Quirk

1

You believe worms fill your guts. Whenever you
eat a meal, you must also swallow a small pebble
to keep them under control.

1

Whenever you become frightened from gaining
Insanity, you let loose a primal scream that might
attract attention.

2

You feel compelled to eat handfuls of grass. Once
you’ve eaten a few, the compulsion ends until
after you complete a rest.

2

When you become frightened from gaining
Insanity, you must use an action during your next
turn to pull out a handful of your hair.

3

Whenever you gain 1 Insanity or more, you must
also get a success on a Will challenge roll with 1
bane or suffer hysterical blindness until you are no
longer frightened from gaining the Insanity.

3

You release a really evil cackle anytime someone
cracks even the tiniest of jokes.

4

Whenever you would go mad and roll a 10 on
the madness table, you become convinced that
your hair is made of snakes. Each round until the
madness ends, you must attack yourself with an
edged or pointed weapon.

5

You believe your skin is drying out and,
sometimes, see it falling and peeling off your
body.

6

Every drink you take tastes like liquor. If you have
half your maximum Insanity or more, you actually
become drunk from drinking even ordinary liquids.

7

You find clothing and armor too constrictive.
While you are frightened from gaining Insanity,
you must use an action each round to remove
your clothing and armor until you are naked or
you remove the frightened affliction.

8

The color blue frightens you. You treat blue
creatures and objects as if they had the
frightening trait.

9

You become angry whenever anyone mentions
the ocean or sea-dwelling creatures.

10

You develop an aversion to certain smells—baked
goods, tobacco, dung, or something else.

11

Whenever you see a shiny object, you must get a
success on a Will challenge roll or, when you are
next able, be forced to move toward that object.

12

You hate certain geometric configurations.

4

Whenever you gain 1 Insanity or more, you must
also get a success on a Will challenge roll with 1
bane or suffer hysterical deafness until you are no
longer frightened from gaining the Insanity.

5

While you are frightened from gaining Insanity,
you cannot speak or make any sounds except for
small gibbering noises.

6

You sometimes burst into song about whatever’s
happening at the time, even really mundane stuff.

7

You always feel the urge to lick the nearest object
to you.

8

Whenever you gain 1 Insanity or more, you
immediately void your bladder and bowels.

9

You chew and pull on your fingernails. If you go
mad and roll a 10, you do not suffer Violence.
Instead, you must spend an action each round
until the madness ends to pull a fingernail from
your finger.

10

You use your finger to constantly probe at your
teeth. If you go mad and roll a 10, you do not
suffer violence. Instead, you must spend an action
each round until the madness ends to free a tooth
from your mouth. If you have no teeth remaining,
you must instead attempt to pull the teeth from
the creature nearest to you.

11

2

Quirk

originalText:
Table 2: Quirks

While you are frightened from gaining Insanity,
you hop instead of walk or run. Halve your Speed
until you remove the frightened affliction.

12

You experience a striking and uncontrollable urge
to dance whenever you speak.

13

While you are frightened from gaining Insanity,
you run around on all fours or on your hindlegs if
you’re a quadruped. Halve your Speed and grant
1 boon on attack rolls made against you until you
remove the frightened affliction.

13

You feel compelled to burn every hat you can see.

14

If ever a specific animal, such as a dog, cat, or
mouse, crossed your path, you immediately fall
prone and refuse to stand up for 1d3 rounds.

15

You refuse to climb ladders or anything remotely
resembling a ladder.

16

At the end of each round you are frightened from
gaining Insanity, roll a d6. If you roll a number
other than 2, 3, or 5, you become stunned until the
end of the next round.

14

While you are frightened from gaining Insanity,
you can only bark like a dog, or imitate another
animal.

17

15

You reveal deep, dark secrets during periods of
prolonged silence.

You cannot keep any kind of secret, even
harmless ones.

18

16

The first word you hear spoken after you
complete a rest becomes your Word of the Day.
Any time you hear it spoken, you must act like an
offensive stereotype of the person who spoke it
for 1 minute.

17

Every time you see a bird you shit your pants.

You suffer from a compulsion to masturbate.
If you have sexual organs, whenever you are
frightened from gaining Insanity, you are also
impaired for as long as you remain frightened. If
you go mad, you become defenseless from your
vigorous masturbation instead of rolling on the
Madness table until you roll a 5 or higher on a d6
at the end of a round.

18

Whenever you become frightened from gaining
Insanity, you see random bursts of light exploding
from your various body parts, which imposes 1
bane on all Perception rolls you make.

19

While frightened from gaining Insanity, you must
move on each turn you take, moving in a circle.

20

You find you can now only speak in rhyme.

19

You believe direct sunlight is bad for you. While
you are frightened from gaining Insanity, you are
impaired while in areas lit by sunlight.

20

You speak in a strange, grating voice others tend
to find irritating.

--- PDF p. 3 ---

originalText:
Table 3: Quirks
d20

d20

Quirk

1

You sometimes pick fights, even without cause.

1

You cannot stand to look at meat of any kind.

2

You believe hair grows spontaneously all over
your body. You shave constantly.

3

You sometimes lose feeling in places on your
body.

4

You are easily distracted by spinning objects,
often at the worst time. You are impaired while
you can see an object spin.

5

Whenever you see a flash of light, such as from
a casting of a Celestial spell, you must get a
success on a Will challenge roll or fall prone and
become unconscious for 1 minute or until you
take damage or another creature uses an action
to shake you awake.

6

You completely neglect your body and
possessions. You are filthy and your possessions
rot or rust away.

2

You say only the opposite of what is true.

3

You break any fragile thing you hold.

4

You sometimes leave strange doodles of an
offensive nature on surfaces without realizing it.

5

You cannot lie.

6

You make very strange, orgasmic noises while
doing mundane, non-sexual things.

7

You believe you can fly and might try to prove it
when given a chance.

8

Choose a color. You make attack rolls against
creatures and objects wearing or of the chosen
color with 1 boon.

9

Whenever you gain Insanity, you must make a Will
challenge roll. You fall prone and become asleep
on a failure, or become fatigued for 1 round on a
success.

10

While you are frightened, you can only speak
words and phrases backwards.

11

Whenever you take damage, you start weeping
uncontrollably.

7

You can no longer see the color green.

8

You become so uneasy that unless you are
wearing medium or heavier armor, you are
impaired.

9

You become unable to detect sarcasm or rhetoric.
You say everything with extreme sarcasm, or
phrase your statements as rhetorical questions.

12

You must always jump feet first into passing
bodies of water, whether lakes or puddles.

10

originalText:
Table 6: Quirks
d20

Quirk

1

You lose all memory of events before a set time in
your life.

2

You completely forget a specific event in your
past.

3

You cannot “split poles.” For example, you
cannot walk past the same object on the
opposite side of another without retracing your
steps or performing some elaborate ritual.

4

You can only walk backwards; take a –4 penalty
to Speed.

5

You have an uncontrollable urge to knock things
off tables.

6

You cannot abide closed doors. You will demolish
them using whatever means necessary.

7

You develop a random stutter.

8

You can only speak if you’re wearing a hat.

9

Whistling noises are irritating and distracting
to you, imposing 1 bane on all attack rolls and
challenge rolls you make while you hear them.

10

You vomit at random times and for no reason.

11

While you are frightened, you believe that
whatever you are wearing is infested with snakes,
spiders, or something worse, which increases the
number of banes imposed on your attack rolls
and challenge rolls by 1.

12

You can’t abide fitted or tight clothing. You
always wear big, baggy items that seem to
swallow you up.

13

You believe you have been a victim of an assault
by a plant. You make attack rolls against plants,
animate or otherwise, with 1 boon, but you grant
1 boon to attack rolls made by plants.

6

You experience severe vertigo while you are
frightened. When you gain this affliction, you fall
prone and can only move by crawling until you are
no longer frightened.

7

If you are touched or take damage while you
are frightened, you must get a success on a Will
challenge roll with 1 boon or fall prone and become
defenseless for 1d3 rounds, during which time you
suffer a full-blown seizure.

8

You develop an annoying need to narrate
everything as it happens around you.

9

Whenever you hear a bell ring, you are compelled
to dig a hole with your bare hands. You dig the
hole in something, such as the ground, or someone,
whether hard or not. You cannot use actions until
you have dug a 5-inch-deep hole.

10

You suffer from severe auditory hallucinations while
you are frightened. You make all Perception rolls
that involve hearing with 2 banes until you are no
longer frightened.

14

11

You suffer from severe visual hallucinations while
you are frightened. You make all Perception rolls
that involve sight with 2 banes until you are no
longer frightened.

originalText:
You sometimes think objects you hold grow hot
or cold. Whenever you roll a 1 or a 20 on a d20
roll made as part of an attack, you drop whatever
you are holding.

15

You speak in odd, affected accents for no reason
at all.

12

Whenever someone laughs, you feel compelled to
slap them in the face.

16

13

You believe you cannot take damage and shrug off
any injury or wound you suffer to be nothing more
than a minor scratch.

You believe that you have developed an allergy
to gold. Your belief is so strong, you are impaired
while you are in contact with the metal.

17

14

You can’t wink. If you try, your eye becomes stuck
closed until you use an action to open it.

Each day at dusk, you fall prone and become
unconscious until dawn. Nothing else can wake
you up. You have come to believe that you are a
vampire, despite lacking any other trait associated
with vampirism.

15

You believe you become invisible whenever you are
frightened and behave as if you were invisible until
you are no longer frightened.

18

You suffer from visceral reliving of traumatizing
memories. You make Will challenge rolls to resist
gaining Insanity with 2 banes.

16

You become incredibly angry when frightened. The
banes imposed on your attack rolls from the affliction
increase by 1, but your attacks deal 1d6 extra damage.

19

17

You experience weird, out-of-body dreams that see
you transported to strange places. Sometimes these
dreams reveal true places, but not always.

You believe you have been cursed. So strong
is this belief that you grant 2 boons on attack
rolls made by other creatures to attack you with
Curse spells and you make challenge rolls to resist
Curses with 2 banes.

20

18

You have an irrational fear of water. Whenever
you are splashed with water or forced into it, you
become frightened until you dry yourself off.

19

You believe you can see into the future and you
thus make prophetic announcements all the time,
though they rarely, if ever, come to be true.

You suffer from dreadful nightmares that prevent
you from getting any benefit from resting unless
you perform a special ritual first. Examples
include having someone wrap you tightly in a
blanket, singing a strange song as loudly as you
can, or emptying your stomach by any means
you can devise.

20

You must touch any and every upright structure
you pass—whether a tree, house, or particularly
large rock. You will run out of your way to do this.

The book is infested with toothy parasites. A creature that
opens the book must get a success on an Agility challenge
roll with 1d3 banes or take 1d6 damage from the burrowing
parasites. At the end of each round, the creature must get
a success on a Strength challenge roll with 1 bane or take

takes 10 damage or more from ﬁre, the eﬀect ends.

The book bears a magical trap. Finding the trap requires
a success on a Perception challenge roll with 3 banes. A
creature with an academic profession involving magical
knowledge makes the roll with 1 boon. Reading any words
in the book causes it to explode in ﬂames. The book and
everything within short range of it takes 3d6 damage. A
creature that gets a success on an Agility challenge roll
takes half the damage instead.

place of an appendage) that attacks any creature that
handles it.

originalText:
Heir Fanatic
Most members of the Heirs count as fanatics. These people
burn with patriotic indignation and believe that they will,
like their ancestors before them, throw off the chains of
tyranny and remake their land into something greater than
it ever was. Without manipulation, these people would be
ordinary folk, engaged in any occupation and with their
whole lives before them. Falling under the leader’s spell has
uprooted them from their lives to take up arms for this holy
cause.

HEIR FANATIC

DIFFICULTY 1

Size 1 human
Perception 9 (-1)
Defense 12 (hard leather); Health 11; Insanity 1d3 - 1;
Corruption 0
Strength 11 (+1), Agility 10 (+0), Intellect 9 (-1), Will 9 (-1)
Speed 10
Strength in Numbers When within short range of 5 or more
creatures friendly to them, an heir fanatic makes attack
rolls and challenge rolls with 1 boon.

ATTACK OPTIONS
Club (melee) +1 (1d6)

Wyvern Claw
Selected from the most capable and violent members of
the fanatics, the wyvern claws comprise a force of obedient
killers who show no hesitation when called to use force
to deal with the cult’s enemies. Wyvern claws form elite
squads sent to carry out dangerous, even suicidal missions,
but, when not sent out to kill, they protect the cult’s elite
members. Wyvern claws wear the same uniforms worn by
the fanatics except for the bronze wyverns pinned to their
lapels.

WYVERN CLAW

DIFFICULTY 5

Perception 9 (-1)

Strength 12 (+2), Agility 11 (+1), Intellect 9 (-1), Will 11 (+1)
Speed 10
Strength of Conviction A wyvern claw imposes 1 bane on
attack rolls against their Intellect and Will. In addition,
whenever they become charmed, compelled, dazed, or
frightened, make a Will challenge roll. On a success, the
affliction ends.

ATTACK OPTIONS
Flail (melee) +2 with 1 boon (2d6 + 2)

originalText:
Wyvern Eyes
As the membership swells and the Heirs’ popularity grows,
both Dolof Mylen and Cardinal Allora fear enemies might
infiltrate their ranks. It would be nice to think that everyone
who joined shared the same enthusiasm and dedication to
the cause, but the leaders know that the Cult of the New
God has spies everywhere and, worse, the sitting godqueen opposes their presence in Old Edene. To root out
the disloyal members and secret apologists for the New
God, the Heirs formed the Wyvern Eyes to serve as a spy
network.
Eyes have tattooed in the palm of their hands a green eye
with a slitted pupil, which they show to identify themselves
when needed. Most disguise themselves in ordinary
clothing so they can get close to hidden enemies and
discover their secrets. People they find dangerous to the
Heirs’ cause disappear, never to be seen again.

WYVERN EYES

DIFFICULTY 5

Size 1 human
Perception 11 (+1)
Defense 13 (soft leather); Health 21; Insanity 1d3;
Corruption 1d3
Strength 11 (+1), Agility 12 (+2), Intellect 11 (+1), Will 10 (+0)
Speed 10
Fast on their Feet When a wyvern eye deals damage to a
creature, the eye’s movement triggers no free attacks until
the start of their next turn.

ATTACK OPTIONS
Long Knife (melee) +2 with 1 boon (1d6 plus Wicked Slash on
attack roll 20+)
Wicked Slash A flesh-and-blood target becomes impaired for
1 minute. While impaired in this way, the target takes 1d6
extra damage each time it takes damage.

originalText:
Hirelings

Seasoned adventures recognize the value of investing
in a few hirelings to attend to the mundane, day-today tasks. If you’ve sent a demon howling back into
the Void, having to keep your armor polished can feel
a bit anticlimactic. You have better things to do than
fumbling around with a torch, holding the horses’
reins, or looking for lodging the next time you blow
into Crossings. Unless you’re a skinflint, you’re bound
to at least be tempted by the folks out there who make
it their business to ease your way through the next
adventure. These folks, called hirelings, henchmen,
servants, lackeys, and less complementary names,
perform specific services in exchange for financial
remuneration.

originalText:
Recruitment

Player characters might decide to part with some of
their hard-earned gold and silver to take on a few
hirelings to help out during their next adventure,
but where do they look to find such august persons?
Luckily, nearly every town and settlement plays host
to no shortage of individuals looking for work. And
one never has to go far to find suitable help, for these
potential hirelings flock to places where they might
find employment. A quick trip to the docks can elicit
a dozen or more offers to resolve all manner of needs,
from those of hauling and lifting, to those of a more
intimate nature. Similarly, hotels, high-class inns,
coaching stations, and other venues of a like kind
attract the hungry and eager.
The abundance of offers says little about the
quality of the individuals in search of pay. After all,
if they were competent, might they not already have
gainful employment? A discerning employer never
accepts the first offer and takes the time to conduct
a proper interview in order to ascertain the merits
and flaws of the hireling. Doing so weeds out those
with insurmountable defects and ensures one finds
qualified candidates able and willing to perform all
the functions of the job described.
This said, the number of prospective candidates
depends largely on the nature of the work and the
size of the community. Any yokel can be convinced to
hold a lantern for a few coins, but scholars of ancient
esoteric lore don’t often quarter in rude hamlets
on the thinly populated fringe of civilization’s vast
tapestry. Similarly, a seemingly qualified contender
for a difficult and dangerous job in some far-flung
village ought to raise alarms; such people don’t often
wind up in such places without good reason. It pays to
inquire into the interviewee’s history and references to
dodge avoidable shenanigans.

2

Skill and Availability
Each hireling has a skill rating, which determines
their availability and capabilities. The skill rating is
a number from 0 to 5, with 0 being unskilled and 5
being quite proficient. Skill rating 0 characters tend
to be laborers with little to no formal training. A
trained fighter might be skill rating 3 and a magicuser would be 5. The first table that follows shows
sample professions by skill rating, while the second
table shows availability and price using the scale
introduced in Shadow.

originalText:
Hireling Secrets

The most common types of hireling available, these
characters can lug around gear, light and hold torches,
and perform common tasks that require no formal
training. These characters have the clothes on their
backs and little else.

d6

Secret

1

The candidate made a dangerous enemy and needs
to get away quick. The people hunting the character
catch up at some point during the next adventure.

2

The candidate is a thief that plans to rob the hiring
character when convenient.

3

The candidate is poor, disloyal, and resentful. It
starts with half loyalty (see below).

Perception 10 (+0)
Defense 10; Health 10; Insanity d3 – 1; Corruption d3 – 2
Strength 10 (+0), Agility 10 (+0), Intellect 9 (–1), Will 8 (–2)
Speed 10

4

The candidate lied about their skill level. Roll a d3 – 1
to determine the candidate’s actual skill level.

ATTACK OPTIONS

5

The candidate carries a disease that’s contagious.
Choose a fun disease or simply make secret Strength
challenge rolls for each member of the group the
next time they rest in proximity to the hireling to see
if they become infected.

6

The candidate masquerades as a hireling but is in
fact a hired killer sent to murder the hiring character
or someone in that character’s group.

originalText:
Hireling Complications
d6

Complication

1

The hireling is in jail. Paying the debt (3d6 cp) frees
the character to work for you.

2

The hireling is out of town, but returns after 1d3 days.

3

The hireling works for someone else. You will have to
pay double to steal the character away.

4

The hireling has retired. You will have to pay double
to coax the character out of retirement.

5

The hireling can only serve for half of the desired
length of service.

6

The hireling is overqualified for the work, with a skill
rating of 1 higher (maximum 5). The hireling will take
the job but at twice the normal rate.

originalText:
Hiring the Hireling

Once the group finds a suitable candidate, they
negotiate the terms of the employment, which specifies
the duration of the service, the work required, and
payment. You can determine that the group strikes the
deal with the following terms: the employment lasts
until they complete the adventure, the work required
falls within the hireling’s broad capabilities, and the
group must pay for at least three days in advance and
with the rest of the payment due at the adventure’s
conclusion. Longer term employment, delayed
payments, and services beyond those expected for the
hireling’s skill rating ought to involve some negotiation,
which can be resolved through roleplaying as normal.

those of the lower rank. These characters might know

Perception 10 (+0)

Speed 10
Skill Training The hireling has one of the following talents.
• While the hireling is with the group in a wilderness
environment, the group cannot become lost.
• The hireling can spend 1 hour hunting, trapping, or
foraging to provide nourishment for up to 5 people.
• The hireling can use an action to remove the
frightened affliction from one animal it can reach.
• The hireling grants 1 additional boon when using an
action to help.
• Food the hireling prepares allows characters that
complete a rest to heal 1d6 extra damage.
• The hireling makes rolls to drive or pilot with 2
boons.

that can see and hear it within long range by
performing music.

ATTACK OPTIONS
Quarterstaff (melee) +0 (1d6)

Artisans, surgeons, healers, apothecaries, and similar
professions represent trades that require expertise in
a particular field. Hirelings from these professions
command a higher rate of pay than their more
mundane fellows. Skill 2 hirelings also include guards
who have a modicum of training. Arms and armor
must be provided for them as part of their service.

originalText:
Hireling Personality Quirks
d20

Personality

1–2

The hireling exhibits obsessive-compulsive behavior,
counting, touching, or straightening all the time.

3–4

The hireling has nothing positive to say ever. The
character grumbles and complains all the time.

5–6

The hireling idolizes a member of the group and
adopts the character’s mannerisms, sayings, and
body language.

7–8

The hireling spouts aphorisms all the time. A fount
of positivity, the character says such things as “You
can’t soar with the eagles if you’re down scratching
with the turkeys” or “I’m good enough, smart
enough, and, darnit, people like me.”

9–10

The hireling has an “endearing” catch phrase:
“Wasn’t me,” “Yessir, right away sir,” “As you wish.”

11–12

The hireling has a disgusting habit. The character
eats loudly, spends time moving phlegm from its
nose to throat and back again, or has reprehensible
hygiene.

13–14

The hireling always has an angle. If the characters
would just listen, the hireling could make
everything awesome for them.

15–16

The hireling does shoddy work and blames others
when caught.

As the most numerous people in the lands of Rûl, most
hirelings have the human ancestry. This said, one might
hire a changeling in human disguise, an orc down on

her armor out of hock. For hirelings of other ancestries,
simply add their ancestry traits to the statistics box.

originalText:
Background

1–2

Fled from war, plague, or something else and
works as a hireling to get back on their feet.

3–4

After failing in another trade, the hireling took
whatever job was available.

5–6

Becoming a hireling gives the character a way
out from a terrible situation, place to live, or bad
relationship.

7–8

Becoming a hireling is part of a new identity the
character has adopted to escape justice, enemies,
or a vengeful cult.

9–10

The hireling went on a few adventures and has a
hankering to get back into the business.

11–12

The hireling bears a curse that compels service to
other would-be heroes.

13–14

The hireling is looking for something and sees an
opportunity to find it by accompanying the group.

15–16

The hireling has nothing better to do.

17–18

The hireling craves recognition and believes that
working in this way will provide it.

19–20

The hireling has severe amnesia.

originalText:
Hireling Reliability
Hirelings promise much, but their dependability only
goes so far. Poor treatment, bad circumstances, and
certain death can all cause hirelings to break ranks
and flee or, worse, turn on their employers. Good
treatment, pay, a cut of the treasure, and more can
keep hirelings loyal and at your side.

originalText:
Loyalty Loss
Bad circumstances cause hirelings to lose loyalty. Each
time a bad circumstance occurs, deduct the indicated
number from the hireling’s loyalty.

For each hireling, the GM makes a Will challenge
roll. The GM makes the roll with 1 boon if the
hireling’s loyalty is 3 or higher and 1 bane if it is 0. If
a hireling has negative loyalty, it gets an automatic
failure. On a success, the hireling’s loyalty holds for
6 rounds and is not subject to loyalty tests during this
time. On a failure, the hireling’s loyalty drops by 1d3.
If the hireling reaches 0 or lower loyalty, roll on the
Failed Loyalty table to see what happens.

Bad Circumstances

originalText:
Disloyalty
Upon reaching 0, the hireling starts looking for a
way out of the arrangement, taking any opportunity
given to take off. Hirelings at this stage sneak away
during the night, flee in battle, or simply walk away.
If a hireling cannot escape in a safe manner, the
hireling remains, but cannot increase its loyalty above
0. The hireling can, though, go negative in loyalty. For
each 24-hour period it must stay with its employer,
the hireling’s loyalty drops by 1. While in negative
numbers, hirelings work to sabotage their employers
and might, at the GM’s discretion, seek their harm.

originalText:
Testing Loyalty
Even the most constant servants think twice about
throwing their lives away, so hirelings, who normally
have little reason to go above and beyond what their
contract stipulates, most likely flee danger, especially
when said danger could mean their very lives. In

6

situations where the outcome looks dire, the GM
might test the hirelings’ loyalty. Such situations
include, but are not limited to, all of the following.
• A player character becomes incapacitated.
• Another hireling dies.
• Enemy combatants number more than twice the
group’s numbers.
• A player character becomes subject to madness.
• The hireling gains Insanity or becomes frightened.

Good Circumstances

Demon Lord a “shot in the arm.” Each builds on the basic
diseases described in the main rulebook to make them
more varied and complex. Here’s how they work.
After the disease’s name and description, you’ll ﬁnd
the transmission entry. This tells you how the disease
spreads and how to resolve exposure to the disease. Next,
some diseases also include a cure entry, which describes
something, if anything, a creature might use to help
overcome the disease.
The disease’s stages come next. Each has two or more.
A creature that fails to resist the disease after exposure
suﬀers the disease’s stage 1 eﬀect. Over time, the creature
might move to a higher or lower stage
as described in the recovery entry.
Should the creature reach stage 0
(if available), the disease is cured,
however some diseases have
residual eﬀects that show how
the disease ravages the body.
Since these diseases are
especially nasty, as they
should be, I recommend using
them sparingly and only when
the disease has a prominent
place in the adventure.

originalText:
Blood Lung
People living on the shores of bogs and swamps in the
Northern Reach frequently contend with a nasty disease
known as blood lung. While locals boil their water to kill
whatever lives inside of it, someone always comes down
with a hacking cough, blood ﬂecking their lips. Blood
lung thrives in hot and humid lands, especially in the
Bone Marsh.
Transmission A living creature that drinks contaminated
water must, 1d3 days after, make a Strength challenge roll
with 1d3 banes. On a failure, the creature suffers blood
lung’s stage 1 effect.
Cure Mother’s mercy, an uncommon herb found in high
mountains or purchased from a reputable apothecary for
1d6 cp, has proven useful in ﬁghting the disease. Ingesting
the leaves grants 3 boons to challenge rolls made to
recover from the disease.
Stage 0 The creature becomes immune to blood lung but
suffers the residual effects.
Stage 1 The creature is diseased. While diseased in this way,
the creature heals half damage.
Stage 2 As stage 1, and whenever the creature gets a failure
on an attack roll or challenge roll, it becomes dazed for 1
round from a coughing ﬁt.
Stage 3 As stage 1. In addition, the creature is slowed and
whenever it gets a failure on an attack roll or challenge
roll, it becomes defenseless for 1 minute from a severe
coughing ﬁt.
Stage 4 The creature takes damage equal to its healing rate
and moves back down to stage 3.
Recovery Each time a creature diseased in this way
completes a rest, it must make a Strength challenge roll.
• 20 or more: The creature moves down one stage.
• Success: No change.
• Failure: The creature moves up one stage.
• 0 or less: The creature takes damage equal to its
healing rate and moves up one stage.
Residual Effects A creature that recovers from Blood Lung
makes all challenge rolls to resist suffocation with 2 banes
due to the scarring of its lungs.
